hook: From Valdespino, one of the classic Sherry houses of Jerez, aged at least two years in barrel.
pitch: This is a bone-dry, light Sherry with a salty, tangy edge, served nicely chilled in a small 100ml glass. It's brilliant before a meal or with oysters and anything salty, and it really wakes up your appetite.
taste: Bone dry, light and tangy, with a salty, almost sea-breeze edge and a gentle nutty, bready note.

dishes.why: The salty, tangy Sherry matches the salt of the oysters and the sharpness of the mignonette without swamping them.
A bone-dry, tangy glass cuts through the salty, fatty cured meats and keeps you coming back for more.
The fresh, salty tang slices through the rich, smoky pâté and keeps each bite feeling light.

hook: Our best-value white at £32: a Sicilian blend of two local grapes, Catarratto and Inzolia.
pitch: This is an easy, light dry white from Sicily, with gentle citrus and orchard-fruit flavours and nothing heavy or showy about it. It's a great-value bottle to share over nibbles or lighter dishes, and it's the most affordable white we have.
taste: A light, dry, easy-drinking white with soft lemony freshness and gentle apple and pear fruit.

dishes.why: An easy Italian white with fried cheese and tomato sauce: it freshens your mouth between bites without fighting the marinara.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: Light and dry, it cuts through the batter and keeps the whole plate tasting fresh.
A gentle white that sits nicely with delicate fish and mussels and doesn't drown them.

hook: Pure Nero d'Avola from hot Sicily, and the lowest-priced red on our list at £32.
pitch: It's a soft, medium-bodied red with ripe dark cherry and plum and a gentle touch of spice. It's easy to drink, great with hearty pub food, and the best-value red bottle we have.
taste: Ripe dark cherry and plum, soft and smooth, with a little spice and a gentle grip.

dishes.why: The ripe dark fruit and gentle grip (that slightly drying feel, called tannin) stand up to the beef and melted cheese.
An Italian red with tomato sauce is a natural match, and its fruit handles the rich fried cheese.

dishes.dish: Black Pudding Scotch Egg, Chop Sauce
dishes.why: Its soft, ripe fruit is a good match for the rich, spicy black pudding.

hook: Our alcohol-free sparkling rosé from the South of France: £6 a glass, £36 a bottle.
pitch: This is a pink sparkling wine with no alcohol, light and fresh with soft red-berry fruit and gentle bubbles. It is perfect if you are driving or skipping alcohol but still want something special in your glass.
taste: Light and fresh, with strawberry, a touch of citrus, gentle bubbles and just a hint of sweetness.
serve: 6-8°C, well chilled · white wine glass or flute

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: It is light and fresh, so it won't cover the delicate raw fish, and its citrus note suits the lemon and dill.
A gentle, fruity fizz with no alcohol is a lovely brunch drink that freshens up the creamy avocado and eggs.

dishes.dish: Whipped Greek Yoghurt, House Granola, Seasonal Berries, Raw Honey
dishes.why: Its red-berry flavour and hint of sweetness pick up the berries and honey.

hook: A Sicilian white from a hot Mediterranean island, and our lowest-priced white by the glass.
pitch: It's a fresh, easy-going dry white from Sicily, usually with lemon and ripe fruit and a clean finish. At £8.50 a glass it's great value and lovely with anything fried, like the fish and chips.
taste: Usually dry and fresh, with lemon, ripe orchard fruit and a clean, easy finish.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: A fresh, dry white refreshes your mouth between bites of crispy batter and goes nicely with the tartare sauce.
An Italian white with Italian flavours, and its freshness cuts through the rich, melting cheese.

dishes.dish: Chicken Milanese, Brown Butter, Capers, Anchovies
dishes.why: Its clean citrus lifts the fried chicken and sits happily with the salty capers and anchovies.

hook: Famille Perrin also make our Viognier, Maison Les Alexandrins; this rosé is usually Grenache-led.
pitch: It's a dry, fresh rosé from the Rhône Valley in France, with light red berry fruit and a little hint of white pepper. It's easy to enjoy on its own or with nibbles, and at £9 it's the best-value glass of rosé we pour.
taste: Dry, fresh and light, with strawberry and raspberry fruit and a little hint of white pepper.

dishes.why: Its freshness cuts through the fried cheese, and its red berry fruit sits happily with the tomato sauce.
A dry, fruity rosé refreshes you between bites of salty cured meat.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: It's light enough not to swamp the delicate fish and goes well with the herbs.

hook: A Syrah from the hot, dry Languedoc in southern France: blackberry fruit with a crack of black pepper.
pitch: It's a full, dark red from the south of France, with blackberry fruit and a twist of black pepper. If you like a bit of spice with grilled meat or game, it's great value at £9 a glass.
taste: Dark and full, with blackberry fruit, a peppery edge and a gentle drying grip at the finish.

dishes.why: Syrah loves game, and its blackberry fruit picks up the blackberries on the plate.
Grilled beef and a peppery red are a classic match, and the grip of the wine cuts through the rich cheese.

dishes.dish: Black Pudding Scotch Egg, Chop Sauce
dishes.why: The black pepper in the wine sits nicely with the spicy, savoury black pudding.

hook: A white from La Mancha in central Spain, and at £38 one of our best-value bottles.
pitch: This is an easy-going dry white from La Mancha in central Spain, the kind of wine that's happy alongside a plate of food rather than demanding attention. At £38 a bottle it's one of the most affordable whites on our list, so it's a relaxed choice for the table to share.
taste: Expect a simple, refreshing dry white of the kind La Mancha usually makes, easy to drink with food.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: A simple, refreshing white is just what you want between bites of crisp batter and tartare sauce.
An easy dry white keeps things fresh against the rich, melting cheese and tomato sauce.
A straightforward white sits comfortably with this cosy potato and cheese pie without overpowering it.

hook: A red from La Mancha in central Spain, and at £38 one of our best-value bottles.
pitch: This is an easy-drinking red from La Mancha in central Spain, a relaxed, crowd-pleasing bottle to share with the food. At £38 it's one of the most affordable reds on our list, so it's a great pick when the table wants something friendly and good value.
taste: Expect a smooth, easy-going red of the kind La Mancha usually makes, with ripe fruit and nothing too heavy.

dishes.why: A friendly Spanish red alongside Spanish pork is an easy, natural match for the rich, slightly sweet meat.
A smooth, easy red is just right with a juicy burger and melted cheese without being too serious.
A soft red works nicely with salty cured meats to pick at before the mains.

hook: A Sauternes, Bordeaux's famous sweet wine, built on Sémillon, a grape prone to sweetness-concentrating noble rot.
pitch: This is a sweet wine from Sauternes in Bordeaux, honeyed and rich with a lovely waxy texture. It is wonderful with blue cheese or a fruit pudding, and at £11 for a 100ml glass it's an easy way to finish the meal.
taste: Sweet and honeyed, with a rich, waxy feel in the mouth and enough freshness to stop it feeling heavy.
serve: 8-10°C · small white or dessert wine glass, 100ml pour

dishes.why: Sweet Sauternes and salty blue cheese are a classic match, and the honeyed wine loves the sweet figs too.
The wine's honeyed richness picks up the honey and pear, and it is sweeter than the pudding, so it never tastes thin.
The rich, waxy wine sits happily with the creamy mascarpone and sweet, nutty tart.

hook: Tawny Port ages in wooden cask, which turns it amber and gives nutty, caramel flavours.
pitch: This is a tawny Port from Niepoort, one of the classic Douro houses: it is aged in wooden casks, so it is amber-brown, sweet and nutty, with caramel and dried-fruit flavours. It is a perfect way to finish, either with a pudding like the pear and walnut millefeuille or with the cheese.
taste: Sweet, smooth and nutty, with caramel, toffee and dried fruit like figs and raisins.

dishes.why: The nutty, caramel flavours of the Port echo the walnuts and honey.
Its dried-fig and nutty flavours mirror the fig and almond in the tart.

dishes.dish: Neal's Yard Cheese Board, Boozy Fruit Chutney, Oat Cakes & Malt Loaf
dishes.why: Sweet, nutty Port is a classic with cheese, and it suits the fruit chutney and malt loaf too.

hook: Malbec from Mendoza's high-altitude desert, where the strong sun makes it softer and riper than in France.
pitch: It's a rich, dark red from Argentina with ripe black plum, blackberry and a hint of violets. It's soft and generous, so it's an easy pick with beef or the burger.
taste: Dark, ripe and smooth, with black plum and blackberry fruit and a floral touch like violets.

dishes.why: Malbec is Argentina's classic red for beef, and its ripe fruit loves rich, savoury meat.
A soft, plummy red is an easy, crowd-pleasing match for a grilled burger.

dishes.dish: Grilled Wing Rib, Bone Marrow, Parsley Butter
dishes.why: Grilled beef is exactly what Malbec is made for, and the bone marrow loves its rich fruit.

say: a-DAY-ga deh mon-SOWNG, VEEN-yo VAIR-day, FRESH-koo
hook: Grown in Portugal's cool, rainy Atlantic climate and made to drink young, just as 'Fresco' on the label promises.
pitch: This is a light, zesty white from Portugal, with lemon and lime, a touch of peach and a salty, sea-breeze edge. It's brilliant with oysters and shellfish, and it's lovely by the glass to start a meal.
taste: Crisp and mouth-watering, with citrus, a little peach and a light salty finish like a sea breeze.

dishes.why: Its salty, citrusy freshness tastes like it belongs next to an oyster.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: Light and lemony, it matches the delicate raw fish and the preserved lemon without drowning them.
This style is made for shellfish, and its freshness lifts the creamy sauce.

hook: Monastrell from warm Alicante: the Spanish name for Mourvèdre, a grape that needs heat to ripen.
pitch: It's a deep, dark Spanish red with blackberry-style fruit and earthy, leathery, slightly gamey notes, and a good firm grip. At £45 it's great value with game or slow-cooked beef, and it tastes of somewhere warm.
taste: Dark fruit with earthy, leathery and gamey notes, deep in colour, with a firm, drying grip.
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant 30 minutes (pour it into a decanter, a glass jug, to soften the young grip)

dishes.why: Its gamey, earthy side matches the venison and its dark fruit picks up the blackberries.

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: Monastrell loves slow-cooked beef, and the rich pie softens its firm grip.

hook: Picpoul is the grape, and it comes from Languedoc, on France's hot, dry Mediterranean coast.
pitch: This is a light, crisp, dry white with a fresh lemony edge, the kind of wine that wakes up your palate. It's lovely with oysters, raw fish or fish and chips, and at £48 a bottle it's a great-value French white.
taste: Light and dry, with zesty lemon and fresh, clean fruit that leaves your mouth watering.

dishes.why: The crisp, lemony freshness works like a squeeze of lemon on a salty oyster.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: It's light enough not to swamp delicate raw fish, and its citrus edge matches the preserved lemon.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: The fresh acidity cuts through the crispy batter and keeps every mouthful tasting clean.

hook: Pieropan is one of the Veneto's classic names, and Garganega gives it almond and citrus blossom notes.
pitch: This is a dry Italian white with soft almond and citrus blossom flavours and a gentle freshness, so it is easy to drink without being sharp. It suits anyone who wants a white that goes with food and won't overpower fish, risotto or a plate of charcuterie.
taste: Dry, light to medium in weight, with almond and citrus blossom flavours and a gentle mouth-watering freshness.

dishes.why: Its gentle freshness and soft almond flavour sit nicely with delicate hake and creamy beans without drowning them.

dishes.dish: Delica Squash Risotto, Brown Butter, Pumpkin Seed Relish
dishes.why: Soave is a natural partner for risotto, and its almond notes echo the nutty brown butter and pumpkin seeds.
Soave is a classic wine with Italian-style cured meats, and its freshness cuts through the salt.

hook: Organic South of France rosé, usually Grenache-led: the grape behind most dry Provençal rosé.
pitch: This is a dry, organic rosé from the South of France, with soft red-berry fruit and a little pinch of white pepper. It's easy to love on its own and friendly with all sorts of food, especially anything with tomato or herbs.
taste: Dry and refreshing, with red berries, a touch of white pepper and a soft, gentle finish.

dishes.why: The red-berry fruit sits nicely with the tomato sauce, and a cold, dry rosé freshens you up between bites of hot, cheesy mozzarella.
Dry rosé with soft berry fruit is a classic match for salty cured meats, refreshing without overpowering them.

dishes.dish: Curried Crab on Malt Rye & Beer Bread
dishes.why: It's light enough for the delicate crab, and the soft fruit calms the gentle spice of the curry.

hook: The grape is Montepulciano from Abruzzo, not related to the Tuscan town of the same name.
pitch: This is a proper Italian red from Abruzzo, full of dark plum and black cherry with a rustic, earthy edge and a firm grip. It has the freshness and backbone to stand up to rich, meaty food, so it really comes alive with dinner.
taste: Dark plum and black cherry with an earthy, slightly rustic edge, fresh acidity and a firm, drying grip from the tannin (the part of red wine that makes your mouth feel dry, like strong tea).

dishes.why: The dark fruit in the wine picks up the blackberries, and its earthy edge loves the venison and celeriac.

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: The firm grip and fresh acidity cut through the rich, slow-cooked beef and bone marrow, so every mouthful feels lighter.
Montepulciano is a classic with pizza and tomato sauces, and its freshness matches the marinara and cuts the fried cheese.

say: fa-MEE-yuh peh-RAN, vee-oh-NYAY, may-ZON lay zah-lex-AHN-dran
hook: A Rhône Viognier: full-bodied, low in acidity and heavily perfumed with apricot and honeysuckle.
pitch: This is a rich, rounded white that smells of apricot, honeysuckle and ripe stone fruit, and it feels soft rather than sharp. If you like a white with plenty of flavour and perfume, especially with gently spiced food, you'll love it.
taste: Ripe apricot, honeysuckle and stone fruit in a full, soft, rounded white with gentle acidity (it isn't tangy or sharp).

dishes.dish: Curried Crab on Malt Rye & Beer Bread
dishes.why: Viognier loves mild spice and creamy curries, and its apricot perfume sits beautifully with the rich, delicate crab.
Its full body matches the rich monkfish, and the perfumed fruit softens the gentle heat of the devilled butter.

dishes.dish: Delica Squash Risotto, Brown Butter, Pumpkin Seed Relish
dishes.why: A soft, full white like this matches the creamy, sweet squash and the nutty brown butter.

hook: Carignan from the South of France: lively and earthy, the grape for hearty stews and cassoulet.
pitch: This is a young red from the South of France made from Carignan, with bright red fruit, lively freshness and a rustic, earthy edge. It's made for hearty food, so it's lovely with our pie, burger or grilled meat.
taste: Red fruit with an earthy, rustic edge, lively acidity and a firm young grip from the tannin (the part of red wine that makes your mouth feel dry, like strong tea).

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: Carignan is a natural with hearty stews, and its lively freshness cuts right through the rich braised beef and bone marrow.
It's a grilled-meat wine, and its firm grip and freshness handle the rich beef and melted cheese.

dishes.dish: Grilled Wing Rib, Bone Marrow, Parsley Butter
dishes.why: Grilled red meat is a classic Carignan match, and the acidity keeps the bone marrow and butter from feeling heavy.

hook: Chiroubles is one of Beaujolais' ten crus, the top named villages, and it's pure Gamay.
pitch: This is a light, juicy red from one of Beaujolais' ten top villages, full of bright strawberry and cherry with very soft tannins, so there's hardly any drying feeling. It's lovely served slightly cool and so easy with charcuterie or roast chicken.
taste: Light and juicy, with bright strawberry and cherry, very little drying grip and sometimes a gentle banana-like note.

dishes.why: Light, juicy Gamay is a classic with cured meats, and the soft tannins won't clash with the salt.
Roast chicken and Beaujolais are a natural pair, and the bright fruit lifts the savoury skin.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: The red fruit and freshness cut the richness of the terrine and pick up the fruity chutney.

hook: Marlborough's sunny days and cold nights lock in the zingy freshness and cut-grass smell.
pitch: This is a zesty New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc, full of gooseberry, passionfruit and that fresh cut-grass smell, with mouth-watering acidity (the lively, refreshing tang that makes your mouth water). If you like a crisp, fresh white that wakes up your food, especially seafood, salads and anything with green herbs, you'll love it.
taste: Zesty and fresh, with gooseberry, passionfruit and a smell of freshly cut grass.

dishes.why: Sauvignon Blanc is a classic with shellfish, and its zingy freshness matches the salty oysters and the sharp mignonette, a vinegar and shallot dressing.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: The wine's high acidity keeps up with the preserved lemon, and its grassy, herby side picks up the dill.
Sauvignon Blanc loves salads, and its freshness stands up to the tangy vinaigrette without tasting flat.

hook: Cubitt House's own-label Chianti from Tuscany, usually Sangiovese, the grape behind most Tuscan reds.
pitch: It's a fresh, medium-bodied Italian red with sour cherry, dried herbs and a savoury, earthy edge, and it has lively acidity, the mouth-watering freshness that makes you want another sip. It's made for food, especially anything with tomato, and at £12 a glass it's an easy, friendly red to enjoy all evening.
taste: Tangy sour cherry and dried herbs with a savoury, earthy finish and a gentle grip on the gums.

dishes.why: Chianti and tomato are a classic match, because the wine's fresh acidity keeps up with the tangy sauce and cuts through the fried cheese.
Grilled beef is a Tuscan favourite with Sangiovese, and the wine's freshness and gentle grip cut through the rich, melted cheese.
The savoury, herby flavours and fresh acidity sit beautifully with salty cured meats and refresh the palate between slices.

hook: Grenache from McLaren Vale, a warm, Mediterranean-style corner of South Australia cooled by the sea.
pitch: This is a ripe, generous Australian red, packed with red berry fruit and a touch of white pepper. It's soft rather than drying, so it's easy to drink and lovely with roast pork, burgers or the venison.
taste: Juicy ripe red berries with a hint of white pepper, warm and soft, with very little drying feel on the gums (that drying feel is called tannin).

dishes.why: Grenache loves roast meat, and its ripe red fruit matches the pork's rich, slightly sweet flavour.
The red berry fruit picks up the blackberries, and the soft texture suits lean grilled venison.
Grenache is a natural with grilled, barbecue-style meat, and its juicy fruit stands up to the rich burger and cheese.

grapes: Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca, Tinta Roriz
say: KEEN-tah duh VAHL duh PEE-oosh, esh-koo-mun-GAH-doo
hook: A dry red from Portugal's Douro, the home of Port, usually made from the same grapes.
pitch: It's a big, dry Portuguese red with concentrated black fruit, a floral hint of violets and firm tannin, the dry grip you feel on your gums. It's built for rich meat dishes, and at £52 a bottle it's a lot of wine for the money.
taste: Dark, concentrated black fruit and violets with a firm, drying grip and a long finish.

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: Douro reds are made for slow-cooked meat, and the firm grip and dark fruit stand up to the rich beef and bone marrow.
The black fruit in the wine picks up the blackberries, and its weight matches the earthy, gamey venison.
Roast beef softens the wine's firm tannin, so both taste rounder and richer together.

say: mee-SHELL duh-loh-MOH, MUSS-kuh-day SEV-ruh ay MEN, soor LEE
hook: 'Sur lie' means it rests on its spent yeast after fermentation, giving extra texture and a slight spritz.
pitch: This is a light, bone-dry white with sharp, refreshing acidity, a gentle softness from resting on its yeast, and a faint prickle on the tongue. It's the classic French wine for oysters and shellfish, so it's perfect with our oysters or the hake with mussels.
taste: Light and bone-dry, with crisp, mouthwatering acidity, a subtle smooth texture and a faint prickle of spritz.

dishes.why: Muscadet is the classic oyster wine: its crisp acidity and clean, salty-fresh feel suit raw shellfish perfectly.
Light enough for delicate hake and mussels, with a gentle texture that matches the creamy beans.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: Its neutral, crisp style lets the delicate raw fish shine while matching the lemony sharpness.

hook: Our own-label Maison Cubitt rosé, from Côtes de Provence: pale, dry and made to drink young.
pitch: This is our own house rosé, a pale, dry rosé from Côtes de Provence with soft red berries and a hint of white pepper. It's the classic Provence style, light and refreshing, and lovely with lighter dishes or just on its own.
taste: Pale and dry, with gentle red-berry fruit, a little white pepper and a clean, refreshing finish.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: A pale, dry Provence rosé is light enough not to swamp the raw fish, and it sits happily with the lemon and dill.
Provence rosé and herby, salty nibbles are a natural pair, just right for a first glass.
The dry red-berry fruit refreshes you between slices of salty cured meat.

hook: 'Alte Reben' is German for old vines; Mosel Riesling grows on steep slate slopes above the river.
pitch: This is a German Riesling from the Mosel: bright and aromatic, never tastes of oak, and has the high, mouth-watering acidity (the lively tang that makes your mouth water) Riesling is loved for. It's brilliant with spicy food and pork, and it keeps everything tasting fresh between bites.
taste: Bright and aromatic, with lively, mouth-watering acidity and no oak flavour.

dishes.dish: Curried Crab on Malt Rye & Beer Bread
dishes.why: Riesling is a classic with spicy food, and its freshness cools the curry heat and cuts through the rich crab.
Riesling and pork are a classic match, and its acidity cuts the richness while its aromatic fruit suits the pork's sweetness.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: Its high acidity cuts through the rich terrine and sits happily with the sweet, spiced chutney.

hook: A pale, dry Côtes de Provence rosé, made to drink young, and ours is the fresh 2025.
pitch: It's a pale, dry rosé from the Côtes de Provence in the south of France, with delicate red-berry fruit and a clean, refreshing finish. It's made to be enjoyed young and fresh, so it's lovely on its own or with lighter dishes like the sea bream crudo.
taste: Pale and dry, with light red-berry fruit, a hint of white pepper and a clean, fresh finish.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: A light, dry rosé won't swamp the delicate raw fish, and it's a Mediterranean wine for a herby, citrusy dish.

dishes.dish: Curried Crab on Malt Rye & Beer Bread
dishes.why: The gentle red-berry fruit and fresh finish sit nicely with sweet crab and a little curry warmth.
It's light enough for delicate hake and mussels, with enough freshness to lift the creamy beans and leeks.

hook: Made from Negroamaro in Salento, Puglia, by Tormaresca, one of the region's classic producers.
pitch: This is an Italian rosé from sunny Puglia, made from the local Negroamaro grape, with riper, rounder red fruit than a pale French rosé. If you'd like a pink wine with a bit more to it for food, it's lovely with the fried mozzarella or the charcuterie.
taste: Dry, with ripe red berries and a rounder, fuller feel than a pale Provence rosé.

dishes.why: An Italian rosé with a bit of weight is a natural match for melting mozzarella and a tomato sauce.
The riper fruit softens the salt in the cured meats, and the freshness keeps each mouthful lively.

dishes.dish: Chicken Milanese, Brown Butter, Capers, Anchovies
dishes.why: It has enough body for the fried chicken and brown butter, and stays fresh against the salty capers and anchovies.

say: la lee-ZHAIR, coht doo ROHN, sood ab-soh-LOO
hook: A Côtes du Rhône, usually Grenache and Syrah; 'Sud Absolu' means 'absolute south' in French.
pitch: This is a warm, smooth French red from the Rhône Valley, full of ripe red berries with a little white pepper on the finish. It has plenty of flavour but is gentle on the gums, so it's easy to enjoy with a rich main like our pie or the beef.
taste: Ripe red berries and a dash of white pepper, warm and rounded, with only a soft drying feel on the gums (that drying feel is called tannin).
serve: 15-17°C · large red glass · decant optional, 20-30 minutes

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: Grenache is a classic with stews and slow-cooked meat, and its soft, peppery fruit sits happily with the rich braised beef and bone marrow.
Roast meats are one of Grenache's best matches, and the red berry fruit freshens each mouthful of beef.
The wine's red berry fruit picks up the blackberries, and its warmth suits the earthy, savoury venison.

hook: Piedmont's everyday red: Barolo must age 38 months, but Dolcetto is usually enjoyed young and soft.
pitch: This is a Dolcetto from Piedmont, the Barolo country of north-west Italy, and it usually tastes of soft dark cherry and plum with a gently bitter almond finish. It's easy-going and food-friendly, so you get proper Piedmont character with your terrine or charcuterie without the weight or the price of a Barolo.
taste: Usually dark cherry, plum and a light bitter-almond twist at the end, soft and smooth rather than sharp.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: The soft dark cherry fruit sits nicely with the rich duck and the spiced pear chutney, and the gentle grip won't fight the terrine.
Dolcetto is a classic Piedmont red with cured meats: its fruit softens the salt and its slight bitterness keeps each bite fresh.
It's juicy and medium-bodied, so it suits a rich burger without feeling heavy.

hook: Tokaj's autumn mists encourage noble rot, a helpful mould that concentrates the grapes' sweetness.
pitch: It's a sweet white from Tokaj in Hungary, tasting of honey and ripe pear and apple, with a lovely fresh zing. It's sweet without ever feeling heavy, so it's perfect with fruit puddings or blue cheese.
taste: Honey and ripe orchard fruit like pear and apple, sweet but kept bright and lively by mouth-watering acidity.
serve: 8-10°C · small white or dessert wine glass (100ml pour)

dishes.why: The wine's honey and pear flavours echo the pudding almost exactly, and its zing keeps the pastry feeling light.

dishes.dish: Bramley Apple Pie, Custard & Soft Serve
dishes.why: The wine's fresh acidity matches the tart Bramley apple and cuts through the creamy custard.
Sweet wine with salty blue cheese is a classic, and the wine's honey sits beautifully with the roasted figs.

hook: Albariño from Rías Baixas, on Spain's cool, wet Atlantic coast, a classic with shellfish.
pitch: It's a crisp, fresh white with citrus, stone fruit like peach and a salty, sea-air edge. If you're having oysters, crab or any fish, it's a natural match, like a squeeze of lemon in a glass.
taste: Zesty lemon and juicy peach with a lick of salt on the finish, clean and refreshing.

dishes.why: Albariño is a classic with shellfish, and its salty, lemony freshness matches the oysters and the sharp mignonette, the vinegar and shallot dressing.
The mussels make this a shellfish dish, and the wine's crisp citrus keeps the creamy beans and leeks tasting light.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: Delicate raw fish needs a fresh, unoaked white, and the wine's citrus picks up the preserved lemon.

hook: Alsace is unusual in France: wines are labelled by grape, so Riesling sits on the label.
pitch: This is a Riesling from Alsace, a sheltered corner of eastern France that stays dry in the shadow of the Vosges mountains, and it's fragrant with a lively, mouthwatering freshness. Riesling is almost never aged in oak barrels, so it lifts rich or spicy food like our Ibérico pork or curried crab rather than weighing it down.
taste: Fragrant and aromatic, with high, mouthwatering acidity (the zingy freshness that makes your mouth water) and a clean finish with no oaky vanilla.

dishes.why: Riesling is a classic with pork, and its fresh acidity cuts through the richness while its fragrance suits the pork's sweetness.

dishes.dish: Curried Crab on Malt Rye & Beer Bread
dishes.why: Riesling is a great match for spicy food, and its zip refreshes your mouth between bites of the curried crab.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: The lively acidity cuts through the rich terrine and sits nicely with the sweet-and-sour spiced pear chutney.

say: la joo-stee-nee-AH-nah, GAH-vee dee GAH-vee, loo-gah-RAH-rah
hook: From Piedmont, home of our Vajra Barolo, but this is crisp white Cortese, and it's by the glass.
pitch: This is a dry, crisp Italian white with clean lemony freshness that wakes up the palate. It's lovely with oysters, raw fish or anything fried, and you can try it by the glass at £14.
taste: Dry, light and crisp, with citrus freshness that makes your mouth water.

dishes.why: Its crisp, lemony freshness works like a squeeze of lemon on salty oysters and stands up to the sharp mignonette.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: A light, crisp white matches delicate raw fish and holds its own against the preserved lemon.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: Its freshness cuts through the batter and keeps every mouthful feeling light.

say: doh-MEN peh-ROH, ma-KON vee-LAHZH, may-ZON KEW-bit
hook: Cubitt House's own-label Mâcon-Villages: Burgundy Chardonnay from Domaine Perraud.
pitch: This is our own Cubitt House white Burgundy, a fresh, clean Chardonnay with citrus fruit and a gently rounded feel. It's easy to love on its own and works beautifully with fish, seafood and roast chicken.
taste: Fresh and clean, with citrus fruit and a soft, gently rounded feel.

dishes.why: A fresh, clean Chardonnay like this is a classic match for oysters and lets their salty, delicate flavour shine.
It's fresh enough for the delicate fish and mussels, with enough roundness for the creamy beans and leeks.
Roast chicken and Burgundy Chardonnay are a natural pairing, and the wine won't overpower the meat.

hook: Chardonnay from Beaujolais, just south of Burgundy and a touch warmer, so the fruit gets riper.
pitch: It's a dry white made from Chardonnay, with ripe apple and citrus fruit and a fresh, mouth-watering finish. If you like white Burgundy, this is a slightly sunnier, rounder take on the same grape from just down the road.
taste: Dry and medium-bodied, with ripe apple and lemon fruit and a fresh, clean finish.

dishes.why: Roast chicken and rounded Chardonnay are a classic pairing, and the fresh finish keeps each mouthful lively.
The ripe fruit matches the creamy beans and leeks without drowning the delicate fish.

dishes.dish: Delica Squash Risotto, Brown Butter, Pumpkin Seed Relish
dishes.why: A rounder white sits nicely with the creamy, nutty risotto, and the freshness stops it feeling heavy.

say: sen-YOR-ee-oh deh PEH peh-THEEN-ya, ree-OH-ha kree-AN-tha
hook: Crianza on a Rioja label means at least two years' ageing, with at least one in oak.
pitch: This is a classic Spanish red, usually made from Tempranillo, with red cherry and plum fruit and a savoury edge from its time in oak barrels. It's easy to enjoy on its own but has enough firmness to stand up to our grilled and roasted meats.
taste: Red cherry and plum with a savoury touch from oak, and a firm, slightly drying feel in the mouth that keeps it from tasting sweet or soft.

dishes.why: Spanish pork with a Spanish red: the cherry and plum fruit suits the rich, slightly sweet meat, and the firmness cuts through the fat.
Rioja is a natural partner for grilled meats, and its red fruit sits nicely alongside the blackberries.
Rioja is a classic with cured meats like chorizo and jamón, and it handles the salt and richness of the board well.

say: rah-OOL PEH-reth men-THEE-ah, ool-TRAY-ah san ZHAHK
hook: Mencía from Bierzo, north-west Spain, by Raúl Pérez, who also makes our Ultreia Godello white.
pitch: This is Mencía from Bierzo in north-west Spain, and it usually tastes of fresh red and dark berries with a floral, slightly peppery edge. It's lively and medium-bodied rather than heavy or oaky, so it's lovely with the venison or the Ibérico pork without wearing you out.
taste: Usually fresh red and dark berries with a floral, slightly peppery lift and a juicy, mouth-watering finish.

dishes.why: The berry fruit picks up the blackberries, and the freshness and medium body match lean venison without smothering it.
A Spanish red with Spanish pork: its juicy freshness cuts through the rich, slightly sweet meat.

dishes.dish: Black Pudding Scotch Egg, Chop Sauce
dishes.why: Its peppery edge and lively acidity stand up to the rich, spiced black pudding.

hook: Austrian Grüner Veltliner from Langenlois, known for a twist of white pepper over citrus.
pitch: It's a crisp, refreshing Austrian white with citrus, a little twist of white pepper and a gentle savoury note. If you like a dry white that wakes up your food, this is a lovely change from Sauvignon or Chardonnay.
taste: Zesty citrus with a pinch of white pepper and a soft savoury edge, a bit like cooked lentils, finishing fresh and dry.

dishes.dish: Chicken Milanese, Brown Butter, Capers, Anchovies
dishes.why: Grüner is the classic wine with schnitzel, and its fresh acidity cuts through the crispy crumb and brown butter.
Grüner is famously good with salads, and its citrus freshness matches the apple and the sharp vinaigrette.

dishes.dish: Curried Crab on Malt Rye & Beer Bread
dishes.why: Grüner suits spiced, Asian-style flavours, and its peppery, zesty character lifts the curry and the sweet crab.

hook: A pale, soft Cinsault from the sunny Languedoc, a grape more often made into rosé.
pitch: It's a pale, light red with soft red berry fruit and hardly any of that drying grip on your gums, so it's very easy to drink. If you'd like a red that won't weigh you down, especially with cured meats or terrine, this is a lovely choice.
taste: Soft, juicy red berries in a pale, light red that feels smooth rather than drying.

dishes.why: Light, soft reds like Cinsault are a classic match for cured meats, and the juicy berry fruit freshens up the salty, rich slices.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: The soft red berry fruit sits nicely with the rich terrine and the sweet chutney without overpowering them.
Roast chicken needs a gentle red, and this one is light and smooth enough to let the chicken shine.

hook: Made by stopping the fermentation with grape spirit, so some of the grapes' natural sweetness stays.
pitch: This is a rich, sweet red Port full of dark black fruit, poured as a 100ml glass. It's lovely with cheese, especially blue cheese, or chocolate puddings, a proper warming way to finish a meal.
taste: Sweet and rich, with ripe black fruit, a hint of violets and a firm, warming grip.
serve: 16-18°C · small wine glass or Port glass

dishes.why: Sweet, dark-fruited Port is a classic with rich, salty cheese, especially if there's a blue.

dishes.dish: Soft Baked Chocolate & Sour Cherry Cookie, Sour Cream Ice Cream
dishes.why: Port's black fruit and sweetness go beautifully with chocolate and cherry.

dishes.dish: Pump Street Dark & White Chocolate Mousse, Salted Caramel, Feuilletine
dishes.why: The rich, sweet Port holds its own against dark chocolate and salted caramel.

hook: A Godello from Bierzo, in north-west Spain, the Spanish white grape many guests haven't tried yet.
pitch: This is a dry Spanish white made from Godello, a grape that usually gives citrus and orchard fruit with a fresh, slightly stony edge and a bit more weight than a light, zippy white. If you enjoy Albariño or white Burgundy and fancy trying something new, this is a lovely discovery.
taste: Usually dry and medium-bodied, with lemon, pear and stone fruit, fresh acidity (that tangy, mouth-watering feel) and a stony finish.

dishes.why: It has enough body for the creamy beans and enough freshness for the hake and mussels.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: Its citrus freshness echoes the preserved lemon without swamping the delicate raw fish.

dishes.dish: Chicken Milanese, Brown Butter, Capers, Anchovies
dishes.why: Its fresh acidity cuts through the fried crumb and brown butter and stands up to the salty capers and anchovies.

say: lay-tahn-DAR duh sha-TOH va-LAD, KEW-bit KLA-ret
hook: Our own-label claret comes from Saint-Émilion, on Bordeaux's Right Bank, where Merlot usually leads the blend.
pitch: It's a soft, rounded red with ripe plum and a touch of cocoa, and it has less of that drying grip than a Cabernet-led Bordeaux. It's our own house claret, available by the glass, and it's lovely with roast pork, duck or anything earthy and mushroomy.
taste: Ripe plum and a little cocoa, smooth and rounded, with a gentle dry finish.

dishes.why: Merlot is a classic match for roast pork, and the plum fruit sits beautifully with the pork's rich, slightly sweet flavour.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: Duck is one of Merlot's best partners, and the soft plum fruit suits the terrine's richness and the sweet chutney.
Merlot loves earthy, mushroomy flavours, so the truffle and creamy root vegetables bring out the wine's smooth, cocoa side.

hook: Our own-label Maison Cubitt red Burgundy, made from Pinot Noir, and poured by the glass.
pitch: This is our own-label red Burgundy, made from Pinot Noir: light and fresh, with red cherry fruit and a gentle earthy note. It's soft and easy to drink, so it works with roast chicken, duck and even fish, and you can have it by the glass.
taste: Light and fresh, with juicy red cherry and a soft earthy note, a bit like a walk in the woods.

dishes.why: Roast chicken is a classic match for Pinot Noir, and the wine's freshness keeps the rich, savoury meat tasting light.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: Duck and Pinot Noir are made for each other, and the wine's fresh acidity cuts through the richness of the terrine.
The wine's gentle earthy note picks up the earthy truffle and artichoke, and its freshness cuts the creamy gratin.

hook: A classic Mediterranean seafood white from Sardinia, usually fermented in steel tanks to keep it fresh.
pitch: It's light and crisp, with citrus and herbs and a faint bitter almond note at the end. If you're having oysters, crudo or any fish, it's the classic Mediterranean seafood white and keeps every mouthful fresh.
taste: Light and crisp, with lemony citrus, fresh herbs and a faint bitter almond finish.

dishes.why: The crisp acidity and citrus work like a squeeze of lemon on salty oysters.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: The wine's citrus and herbal notes echo the preserved lemon and dill without swamping the delicate fish.
It's a light seafood white, so it freshens up the creamy beans and leeks and loves the mussels.

say: veen-YOH-bluh ghee-OHM, kray-MON la FLOOT on-shon-TAY
hook: French sparkling wine from Franche-Comté, usually Chardonnay, and our least expensive French bottle of fizz.
pitch: This is French sparkling wine from outside Champagne, crisp and lemony with lively bubbles. It gives you a proper celebration bottle at £65, a lot less than Champagne.
taste: Expect crisp, lemony fruit and lively bubbles, usually lean and fresh rather than toasty.

dishes.why: Crisp, unoaked Chardonnay is a classic partner for oysters and their sharp mignonette.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: The bubbles and fresh acidity cut through the batter and keep each mouthful feeling light.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: Its lemony freshness echoes the preserved lemon and doesn't overpower the delicate raw fish.

hook: White Rioja from Spain's top-tier DOCa region, where the Ebro valley tempers the climate with Atlantic air.
pitch: This is the white side of Rioja, a young 2025 usually made from the Viura grape, dry and fresh. If you love red Rioja, it's a lovely way to try the same region with fish, chicken or a salad.
taste: Usually dry and fresh, light to medium in body, with gentle orchard fruit and a clean finish.

dishes.dish: Chicken Milanese, Brown Butter, Capers, Anchovies
dishes.why: A fresh, dry white cuts through the fried crumb and brown butter and is happy alongside the salty capers and anchovies.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: Its freshness keeps the batter and chips feeling light, the way a squeeze of lemon would.
A dry, gentle white sits nicely with the fresh apple and earthy celeriac without fighting the vinaigrette.

hook: A pale, dry Côtes de Provence rosé from a hot, dry Mediterranean spot, made for drinking young.
pitch: It's a pale, dry rosé from Côtes de Provence, so not sweet at all, with gentle red berry fruit and a little hint of white pepper. It's made to be drunk young and fresh, so it's lovely on its own or with lighter fish and herby dishes.
taste: Pale and dry (not sweet), with light red berry fruit and a touch of white pepper.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: A pale, dry rosé is gentle enough for delicate raw fish and sits nicely with the lemon and herbs.
Its light red berry fruit refreshes alongside the creamy, delicate fish and shellfish without drowning them.
Dry rosé with a touch of pepper is a classic, easy partner for salty cured meats.

hook: From the warm, Mediterranean south of the Rhône, where Grenache gives red berries and white pepper.
pitch: It's a warm, generous red from the south of France, usually Grenache with some Syrah, full of ripe red berries with a little white pepper. It's smooth rather than drying, so it's very easy to enjoy with hearty dishes like our pie or roast beef.
taste: Ripe red berries and a hint of white pepper, with a warm, rounded feel and soft tannin, so it doesn't dry your mouth out.

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: Southern Rhône reds are made for stews and braises, and the ripe fruit and warmth match the rich beef and bone marrow.
Roast meats are a classic match, and the soft tannin and peppery fruit work beautifully with the beef.
The ripe red berry fruit picks up the blackberries, and there's enough body for the grilled venison.

hook: Spätburgunder is simply the German name for Pinot Noir; this one's a 2021 from Rheinhessen.
pitch: Spätburgunder is what the Germans call Pinot Noir, so expect a light, fresh red with red cherry fruit and a gentle earthy note. It's soft and silky with hardly any drying grip, so it's lovely with duck, game or even fish.
taste: Light and fresh, with red cherry fruit and a soft earthy note, like a walk in the woods.

dishes.dish: Roast Creedy Carver Duck, Orange Sauce
dishes.why: Duck is a classic with Pinot Noir, and the wine's fresh acidity cuts through the rich meat and stands up to the orange sauce.
The wine's red fruit sits nicely with the blackberries, and its earthy side suits the venison.

dishes.dish: Celeriac, Beetroot & Chard Pithivier, Vegetable Gravy
dishes.why: A light, earthy red like this matches the earthy vegetables without weighing them down.

hook: Niepoort is one of the Douro's classic Port houses, and this is their chilled white Port.
pitch: This is a white Port, a wine strengthened with a little grape spirit, so it is golden, nutty and only gently sweet, and we serve it chilled. It makes a lovely before-dinner drink with something salty, like the charcuterie or the mackerel pâté.
taste: Golden and nutty, with soft citrus and dried-fruit notes and a gentle touch of sweetness, served nicely chilled.

dishes.why: The gentle sweetness and nutty flavour balance the salt and richness of the cured meats.
Served chilled, it freshens the palate after the smoky, rich pâté, and its soft sweetness softens the salt.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: Its touch of sweetness picks up the pear chutney, and its nuttiness suits the rich terrine.

hook: A red from the warm southern Rhône, usually led by Grenache: red berries, white pepper, soft and warming.
pitch: It's a warming French red with ripe red berries and a little white pepper, soft rather than drying in the mouth. If you like a red with plenty of flavour that's easy to drink with roast meat, this is a lovely glass.
taste: Ripe red berries and a twist of white pepper, smooth and warming, without much of that dry, mouth-gripping feel.

dishes.why: Grenache-based reds are classic with roast meat, and the soft red fruit sits nicely with rich roast beef.
The red berry fruit picks up the blackberries, and the pepper suits the earthy venison.
It's soft enough not to swamp roast chicken but has enough flavour to stand up to the savoury, roasted skin.

hook: Chardonnay from cool-climate Chablis, the step below our Premier Cru and Grand Cru Chablis.
pitch: This is Chablis, which is Chardonnay from the cool north of Burgundy, so think crisp, clean and citrusy rather than rich and buttery. It's a classic with oysters and white fish, and a really elegant way to start a meal.
taste: Clean and crisp, with lemony citrus and a fresh, lean, dry finish.

dishes.why: Crisp, unoaked-style Chardonnay is the classic wine for oysters, matching their salty freshness and the sharp mignonette (a vinegar and shallot dressing).

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: Its lemony freshness mirrors the preserved lemon without drowning the delicate raw fish.
A lean Chardonnay suits white fish, and its freshness keeps the creamy beans and leeks tasting light.

say: da-VEED mo-RAY, a-lee-go-TAY, luh gron AH
hook: Aligoté, Burgundy's other white grape, by David Moret, who also makes our Meursault and Saint-Romain.
pitch: It's a crisp, dry white from Burgundy made from Aligoté rather than Chardonnay, with bright lemony freshness that makes your mouth water. It's a brilliant wake-up wine with oysters and raw fish, and a fun change for anyone who usually orders Chablis.
taste: Dry, light to medium-bodied and crisp, with lemony, mouth-watering freshness.

dishes.why: A crisp, lemony white is like a squeeze of lemon over a salty oyster.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: Its zesty freshness echoes the preserved lemon and doesn't swamp the delicate raw fish.
The sharp freshness cuts through the rich, smoky fish and refreshes the mouth.

hook: Valpolicella from the Veneto, Amarone country, usually built on Corvina and its tart cherry fruit.
pitch: It's a smooth, medium-bodied Italian red with tart cherry fruit and gentle tannin, so it's easy to enjoy with or without food. It comes from the same corner of Italy as Amarone and is a great partner for our charcuterie or the short rib pie.
taste: Tart cherry fruit in a smooth, medium-bodied red with a gentle grip.

dishes.why: Valpolicella is a classic match for Italian-style cured meats, and the tart cherry fruit cuts through the salt and fat.

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: Valpolicella reds are made for braised beef, and the cherry freshness lifts the rich pie.
The tart cherry fruit echoes the blackberries and the gentle tannin suits lean, grilled venison.

hook: Listed with our whites, not our fizz: an English white from the South Downs, usually Chardonnay.
pitch: This is an English white from the South Downs, usually made from Chardonnay, a grape that picks up whatever the winemaker does with it. If you fancy drinking something English with your fish, it's a lovely choice and a bit of a talking point.
taste: Expect a white from cool English hills, so think fresh and citrusy rather than heavy, but taste it before service so you can describe this bottle in your own words.

dishes.why: Chardonnay is a classic partner for delicate white fish and a creamy sauce, so it sits happily with the hake and mussels.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: A fresh white like this suits delicate raw fish and the lemon and dill.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: A fresh English white cuts through the batter and makes a proper British pairing.

say: jee-dee VYE-rah, LAN-geh neb-YOH-loh, kla-RAY jay-see
hook: Nebbiolo looks pale in the glass but tastes powerful, with real grip and bright freshness.
pitch: This is Nebbiolo from Piedmont in north-west Italy, the grape behind Barolo: pale in the glass, with scents of rose petals and a hint of tar, lively freshness and a firm, drying grip. It is brilliant with rich, slow-cooked beef or game, because that freshness and grip cut straight through the richness.
taste: Rose petals and a touch of tar, with mouth-watering freshness and plenty of tannin, the drying grip you feel on your gums, despite its pale colour.
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant 30 minutes helps soften the grip

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: Braised beef is a classic Nebbiolo match, and the wine's freshness and grip cut through the rich meat and bone marrow.
Game is one of Nebbiolo's favourite partners, and the earthy celeriac suits its rose-and-tar character.
Truffle is a famous Piedmont pairing for Nebbiolo, and the wine's freshness lifts the creamy gratin.

hook: A South African Pinot Noir from the Western Cape: a light red that happily goes with fish.
pitch: This is a light, fresh red from South Africa's Western Cape, with red cherry and a gentle earthy note, like a walk in the woods. It's soft rather than drying, so it's lovely on its own and works with fish as well as meat.
taste: Red cherry with an earthy, forest-floor note, light and mouth-watering, with only a soft, gentle grip.

dishes.why: Monkfish is a meaty fish, and this light, fresh red has the soft grip that lets you drink a red with fish.
Roast chicken and Pinot Noir is a classic match: the red cherry fruit and freshness lift the savoury, crispy chicken.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: Duck is one of Pinot Noir's best partners, and the wine's freshness cuts through the rich terrine.

hook: A 2023 California Chardonnay, a neutral grape that takes on whatever the winemaker does.
pitch: This is a Chardonnay from California, a sunny part of the world that generally gives the grape riper fruit. If you like a rounder white with your chicken or a creamy dish, it's a really easy one to enjoy.
taste: Expect a riper, rounder Chardonnay than our cooler-climate ones, but taste it before service so you can describe this bottle in your own words.

dishes.why: Roast chicken is one of the classic matches for a fuller Chardonnay.

dishes.dish: Delica Squash Risotto, Brown Butter, Pumpkin Seed Relish
dishes.why: A rounder Chardonnay suits a creamy, buttery risotto.
Chardonnay goes beautifully with white fish in a creamy sauce.

hook: Valpolicella's sweet red, usually from Corvina, the grape this corner of Italy famously dries for Amarone.
pitch: It's a sweet red from Valpolicella in north-east Italy, full of dark cherry and raisin with a soft, gentle finish. If you love chocolate or a good cheese at the end of a meal, this gives you red-wine flavour with pudding sweetness.
taste: Sweet dark cherry and raisin, rich and smooth, with a little tartness so it doesn't feel sticky.
serve: 14-16°C · small red or dessert wine glass (100ml pour)

dishes.dish: Soft Baked Chocolate & Sour Cherry Cookie, Sour Cream Ice Cream
dishes.why: The wine's dark cherry picks up the sour cherry in the cookie, and it's sweet enough to stand up to the chocolate.

dishes.dish: Neal's Yard Cheese Board, Boozy Fruit Chutney, Oat Cakes & Malt Loaf
dishes.why: Sweet red with salty, rich cheese is a classic, and the raisin notes sit nicely next to the fruit chutney and malt loaf.

dishes.dish: Pump Street Dark & White Chocolate Mousse, Salted Caramel, Feuilletine
dishes.why: Cherry and chocolate is a match everyone knows, and the wine's freshness keeps the creamy mousse from feeling heavy.

hook: Sancerre is the Loire's Sauvignon Blanc: citrus and a struck-stone 'flinty' edge, made for drinking young.
pitch: This is Sancerre from the Loire Valley, made from Sauvignon Blanc: crisp and zesty, with citrus, a fresh cut-grass, herby note and a 'flinty' edge, a bit like the smell of struck stone. It's made to be enjoyed young and fresh, so it's brilliant with our oysters, the sea bream crudo or a bright salad.
taste: Crisp and zesty, with citrus, cut grass, green herbs and a clean, stony 'flinty' finish.

dishes.why: Sauvignon Blanc is a classic with shellfish, and its crisp citrus freshness is like a squeeze of lemon on the oysters.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: Its herby, citrusy character echoes the dill and preserved lemon without smothering the delicate raw fish.
Sauvignon Blanc loves salads, and its high acidity stands up to the sharp vinaigrette.

hook: Gris is French for grey, after the grape's greyish skin. It's grown in the hot, dry Languedoc.
pitch: This is a fuller, rounder white from the sunny south of France, with ripe pear and soft yellow fruit rather than sharp citrus. If you like a white with a bit of weight that holds its own next to richer dishes, you'll really enjoy it.
taste: Ripe pear and soft yellow fruit, with a rounded, gently warm feel and a smooth, dry finish.

dishes.why: Monkfish is a meaty fish, and this full white has the weight to match it and the spicy butter.

dishes.dish: Delica Squash Risotto, Brown Butter, Pumpkin Seed Relish
dishes.why: The wine's round, ripe fruit sits comfortably with the creamy, sweet squash and nutty brown butter.
Roast chicken loves a fuller white, and this one has the body to go with the rich, savoury meat.

hook: Stellenbosch is warm, but cooled by False Bay; Syrah there brings black pepper and blackberry.
pitch: This is a South African Syrah from Stellenbosch: deep in colour, with blackberry fruit, a twist of black pepper and a firm, drying grip. It's made for grilled meat and game, so it's a lovely match for our venison or the wing rib.
taste: Blackberry and black pepper, with a good firm grip from the tannin, the drying feeling you get on your gums.
serve: 15-17°C · large red glass · decant optional, 20 minutes

dishes.why: Game is a classic Syrah match, and the wine's own blackberry flavour echoes the blackberries on the plate.

dishes.dish: Grilled Wing Rib, Bone Marrow, Parsley Butter
dishes.why: Syrah loves grilled meat, and its grip and peppery edge stand up to the rich beef and bone marrow.
Grilled beef and a peppery red are a simple, crowd-pleasing pairing.

say: TEH-rah dah MAR-kah, KAH-vah broot nah-TOO-rah
hook: Bone dry with no sugar added, from Penedès, where most of Spain's Cava is made.
pitch: This is a properly dry Spanish fizz, crisp and light with citrus and apple, and 'Brut Natura' means no sugar is added at the end, so it's as dry as sparkling wine gets. If you like your fizz clean and refreshing rather than soft or sweet, it's perfect with oysters and anything from the sea.
taste: Bone dry, crisp and light, with lemon, green apple and a gentle savoury, bready edge.

dishes.why: A bone-dry, crisp fizz is the classic match for salty raw oysters and the sharp vinegar dressing.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: It's light enough not to swamp the delicate raw fish, and its citrus freshness echoes the lemon and dill.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: The crisp acidity and bubbles cut through the fried batter like a squeeze of lemon.

hook: White Burgundy from Marsannay: Chardonnay from a cool region where every vintage tastes a little different.
pitch: This is a dry white Burgundy made from Chardonnay, medium-bodied and fresh, from one of France's cooler wine regions. If you like a white with some weight that still feels lively, it's a lovely match for our roast chicken or the hake.
taste: A dry, medium-bodied Chardonnay with the fresh, lively acidity (the mouth-watering tang) you'd expect from Burgundy's cool climate.

dishes.why: Chardonnay with a bit of body is a classic with roast chicken, matching its savoury richness without smothering it.
Chardonnay suits white fish, and this wine's freshness keeps the creamy beans and leeks tasting light.

hook: Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot from Saint-Estèphe, on Bordeaux's gravelly Left Bank, where blends lean towards Cabernet.
pitch: It's a firm, serious red with blackcurrant and cedar, and that drying grip, like strong tea, is exactly what a big plate of beef needs. With fatty red meat the grip softens and the fruit comes forward, so it really comes alive with our steak and pie.
taste: Blackcurrant and cedar with a firm, drying grip and a fresh, mouth-watering finish.

dishes.dish: Grilled Wing Rib, Bone Marrow, Parsley Butter
dishes.why: The fat in the beef and bone marrow softens the wine's grip, and the blackcurrant fruit shines with grilled meat.
Rich roast beef is a classic match for Cabernet, and the meat smooths out the wine's firm, drying edge.

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: This rich, savoury pie has the weight and fat to stand up to a firm, Cabernet-based red.

hook: A Bordeaux white, usually Sauvignon Blanc with Sémillon, from a climate cooled by the Gironde estuary.
pitch: It's fresh and zesty, with gooseberry, passion fruit and a cut-grass note, so it wakes up the palate and makes food taste brighter. If you like a crisp white that loves seafood, salads and herbs, this is a lovely choice, and you can have it by the glass.
taste: Zesty and fresh, with gooseberry, passion fruit and a cut-grass note, and a slightly rounder middle.

dishes.why: Sauvignon Blanc and shellfish are a classic match, and its zesty freshness keeps up with the sharp mignonette, the vinegar and shallot dressing.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: The wine's grassy, herby side picks up the dill, and its freshness matches the preserved lemon.
Sauvignon Blanc loves salads, and its crispness stands up to the tangy vinaigrette.

hook: Domaine Ott is one of the classic names of Provence rosé, alongside Château d'Esclans.
pitch: This comes from Domaine Ott, one of the classic producers of Provence, and it's a pale, dry rosé, so not sweet, with red berry fruit and a little white pepper. It's a lovely bottle to share with seafood or lighter starters, and a real treat if you love Provence rosé.
taste: Pale and dry (not sweet), with red berry fruit and a hint of white pepper.

dishes.dish: Curried Crab on Malt Rye & Beer Bread
dishes.why: A pale, dry rosé with red berry fruit is gentle with the spice and lets the sweet, delicate crab shine.
It's fresh and light enough for delicate fish and mussels in a creamy sauce.
Dry rosé with a touch of white pepper is an easy, classic partner for salty cured meats.

hook: Cabernet Sauvignon's thick grape skins give this California red its deep colour and firm grip.
pitch: It's a deep, dark California red with blackcurrant and a cedar-wood note, and a firm, drying grip on the gums that wine people call tannin. That grip is exactly why it's brilliant with our beef: the fat in the meat softens it, so the wine tastes rounder and the fruit comes through.
taste: Blackcurrant and cedar wood, with fresh acidity (a mouth-watering zing) and a firm, drying grip on the gums.

dishes.dish: Grilled Wing Rib, Bone Marrow, Parsley Butter
dishes.why: Grilled beef is Cabernet's classic partner, and the fat and bone marrow soften its firm grip.
Rich roast beef tames the wine's tannin, and the blackcurrant fruit stands up to the meat.
The burger's fat and the rich cheese soften the wine's grip, so it tastes smoother and fruitier.

say: vyuh koh-LEZH, boor-GOYN ROOZH, coat DOR
hook: Burgundy Pinot Noir from 2022; in Burgundy's cool climate, the year it was picked really matters.
pitch: This is red Burgundy, which means Pinot Noir from its home in France: light and fresh, with red cherry and an earthy, woodland note. It's a proper step up from the house Pinot and goes beautifully with roast chicken, duck or mushrooms.
taste: Red cherry and earthy, forest-floor notes, light in weight, mouth-watering and soft, with very little drying grip.

dishes.why: Roast chicken is a classic partner for Pinot Noir: the fresh red cherry lifts the savoury, crispy chicken without swamping it.

dishes.dish: Roast Creedy Carver Duck, Orange Sauce
dishes.why: Duck is one of Pinot Noir's best matches, and the wine's freshness cuts through the rich meat and sweet sauce.
Pinot Noir loves earthy, mushroomy flavours, so its forest-floor notes sit right alongside the truffle.

hook: English fizz from Hampshire, grown on the same chalk seam that runs under Champagne.
pitch: This is English sparkling wine from Hampshire, made from the same three grapes as Champagne, crisp and lively with apple, lemon and a gentle bready note. It's our English fizz by the glass, so it's an easy way to try something local that's bright, refreshing and brilliant with fried food.
taste: Crisp and lively, with green apple, lemon and a soft, bready, toasty note.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: The high acidity and bubbles cut through the batter like a squeeze of lemon.
Its crispness freshens up the rich, creamy cheese and keeps pace with the tangy tomato sauce.
The sharp acidity slices through the rich, smoky, salty pâté and leaves your mouth feeling clean.

hook: Chenin Blanc from Swartland, South Africa: hot, dry country full of old, low-growing bush vines.
pitch: This is a South African Chenin Blanc with lovely lively freshness and a bit of weight to it, so it feels bright but not thin. It's a great choice with pork or chicken, because the freshness cuts through richness and keeps every mouthful tasting clean.
taste: A fresh, lively white with mouth-watering acidity and a medium weight that feels satisfying rather than light.

dishes.why: Pork is a classic match for Chenin Blanc, and its freshness cuts through the rich, slightly sweet meat.
Roast chicken and Chenin Blanc are a natural pairing, and the wine has enough weight to sit alongside it.

dishes.dish: Curried Crab on Malt Rye & Beer Bread
dishes.why: Chenin Blanc works well with spiced dishes, and its freshness keeps the rich, spicy crab tasting light.

hook: A South African Chardonnay from the Western Cape, made from a grape that reflects its winemaker's choices.
pitch: This is a dry, medium-bodied Chardonnay from the Western Cape in South Africa, a fresh, modern alternative to white Burgundy. If you enjoy Chardonnay, it's a lovely partner for the roast chicken, the hake or the squash risotto.
taste: A dry, medium-bodied white with fresh acidity (the mouth-watering tang), shaped by how the winemaker chose to make it.

dishes.why: Chardonnay with some body is a classic with roast chicken and matches its savoury richness.
Chardonnay suits white fish, and its weight sits nicely with the creamy beans and leeks.

dishes.dish: Delica Squash Risotto, Brown Butter, Pumpkin Seed Relish
dishes.why: A Chardonnay with some body stands up to a creamy, nutty risotto without overpowering it.

hook: Sangiovese from Montalcino in Tuscany, the same place that gives its name to Brunello di Montalcino.
pitch: It's a Tuscan red made from Sangiovese, with sour cherry, dried herbs and a savoury, earthy edge, lively and fresh rather than heavy. If you like a red that makes your mouth water and is brilliant with food, especially tomato dishes or roast beef, you'll love it.
taste: Sour cherry and dried herbs with an earthy, savoury edge, mouth-wateringly fresh, with a moderate drying grip on the gums.
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant optional, 30 minutes

dishes.why: Sangiovese is made for tomato, and its fresh acidity cuts through the rich fried cheese.
Tuscany's classic pairing is grilled steak, and the cherry fruit and gentle grip suit roast beef perfectly.
The earthy, savoury side of the wine matches the earthy venison and celeriac.

hook: From Lalande-de-Pomerol on Bordeaux's Right Bank, where clay soils usually make Merlot the backbone of the blend.
pitch: This is a smooth, plummy red Bordeaux from Lalande-de-Pomerol, usually led by Merlot, so it's softer and rounder than a Cabernet-led Bordeaux, with plum and a touch of cocoa. It's lovely with our roast pork or the beef with wild mushrooms, and the 2019 has a few years of age behind it.
taste: Plum and cocoa, often with a chocolate and vanilla note from oak barrels, and a soft, smooth grip.
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant 30 minutes if there's time

dishes.why: Roast pork is a classic match for Merlot, and its plum fruit and soft grip sit nicely with the rich, slightly sweet pork.

dishes.dish: Roast Yorkshire Beef Rump, Wild Mushrooms & Gravy
dishes.why: Merlot loves mushroom dishes, and the earthy wild mushrooms and gravy bring out the wine's cocoa side.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: Duck is a natural partner for Merlot, and its soft grip won't fight the rich terrine.

hook: Napa Valley Zinfandel: warm days, fog-cooled nights off San Pablo Bay, jammy fruit and peppery spice.
pitch: It's a big, juicy Californian red with jammy black and red fruit and a peppery kick, but it's dry, not sweet. It's made for rich, savoury food like a burger, and it's ready to enjoy right now.
taste: Jammy blackberry and red berry fruit with peppery spice, full and warming, and dry rather than sweet.

dishes.why: Zinfandel is a classic with burgers: the jammy fruit and pepper stand up to the rich, salty beef and cheese.

dishes.dish: Black Pudding Scotch Egg, Chop Sauce
dishes.why: Zinfandel loves spicy sausage, and the ripe fruit and pepper match the rich, spicy black pudding.
The juicy fruit goes with the slightly sweet, rich roast pork.

say: doh-MEN de la bay-GOOD, ban-DOLL roh-ZAY
hook: From Bandol in hot, dry Provence, usually made with Mourvèdre, a grape that needs warmth to ripen.
pitch: This is a pale, dry rosé with more depth than most pinks, with red fruit and a savoury, herby edge. If you love Provence rosé but want something with real substance to drink with food, this is the most serious rosé on our list.
taste: Dry and pale, with red berry fruit, a savoury, herby edge and a fuller feel in the mouth than a typical light rosé.

dishes.why: It's dry with a savoury edge, so it freshens the mouth after salty cured meats without being swamped by them.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: It has enough weight for the rich duck, and its fruit sits nicely with the spiced pear.
A fuller dry rosé is a classic partner for pork, with enough depth for the meat but still fresh.

hook: South Downs English fizz, usually Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, from England's chalk seam shared with Champagne.
pitch: This is an English sparkling wine from the South Downs, fresh and lively with mouthwatering acidity and fine bubbles. If you like Champagne, you'll enjoy it: it comes from the same chalky ground and cool climate, and it's brilliant with anything fried or salty.
taste: Crisp and lively, with citrusy freshness, mouthwatering acidity and fine, creamy bubbles.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: The bubbles and sharp freshness cut through the crispy batter the way vinegar does on chips.
The lively acidity lifts the rich, smoky, salty pâté and keeps every bite tasting fresh.
Fizz and acidity clean the creamy, fried cheese off your palate and stand up to the tangy tomato sauce.

hook: Gusbourne is one of England's classic sparkling houses; this is all Chardonnay, from Kent's 2020 harvest.
pitch: This is English sparkling wine from Kent, made only from Chardonnay, so it's crisp, citrusy and really refreshing. It comes from one of England's best-known sparkling wine producers, and you can have it by the glass, which makes it perfect with oysters or to start the evening.
taste: Crisp, lean and citrusy, with mouthwatering freshness and fine, lively bubbles.

dishes.why: Crisp Chardonnay fizz and salty, delicate oysters are a classic match, and its acidity is as sharp as the mignonette.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: Its citrus freshness echoes the preserved lemon without smothering the delicate raw fish.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: The bubbles and high acidity cut through the batter and keep each mouthful tasting fresh.

say: doh-MEN day AHT, sha-BLEE pruh-MYAY KROO, voh duh VAY
hook: A Premier Cru Chablis: Burgundy's second-highest quality tier, just below Grand Cru, from a cool continental climate.
pitch: This is Chardonnay from Chablis in Burgundy, where the cool weather keeps it dry, fresh and lively, with clean citrus flavours. It's a Premier Cru, one step below the very top, so you get real quality without paying Grand Cru prices.
taste: Dry, fresh and lively, with citrus fruit and a clean, crisp finish.

dishes.why: Chablis and oysters are a classic pairing: the wine's crisp freshness cuts through the salty oysters and the sharp mignonette.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: The wine's citrus freshness picks up the preserved lemon and won't overpower delicate raw fish.
A fresh white like this suits white fish and shellfish, and its lively acidity keeps the creamy beans and leeks from feeling heavy.

hook: South African Pinot Noir from the Cape South Coast, from the same house as our Agnes Chardonnay.
pitch: This is a light, fresh red with red cherry fruit and a gentle earthy note, like damp leaves and mushrooms, and hardly any of that drying grip you get from heavier reds. It's a lovely choice if you want a red that won't overpower your food, and it's light enough to drink with chicken, duck or even fish.
taste: Light and mouth-wateringly fresh, with red cherry fruit and a soft earthy hint of damp leaves and mushrooms.

dishes.why: Roast chicken is one of Pinot Noir's classic partners, and this light red won't drown out the meat.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: Duck loves Pinot Noir, and the wine's freshness cuts through the richness of the terrine.
The wine's earthy, mushroomy side picks up the truffle and earthy vegetables.

hook: Made from grapes left to freeze naturally on the vine, near Lake Ontario in Canada.
pitch: This is a Canadian icewine, made from grapes that freeze naturally on the vine, and it tastes very sweet and rich but with a bright, mouth-watering freshness. It is a real treat with fruit puddings like our apple pie, and the half bottle is perfect for two to share.
taste: Very sweet and rich, like honeyed ripe fruit, with a lively freshness that keeps it from feeling heavy.

dishes.dish: Bramley Apple Pie, Custard & Soft Serve
dishes.why: The wine's freshness matches the tart apple, and its sweetness stands up to the custard and soft serve.
Honeyed sweetness with pear and honey makes an easy, lovely match.
Very sweet wine with salty blue cheese is a classic pairing, and the figs bring them together.

hook: English pink fizz from Hampshire, grown on the same chalk seam that runs under Champagne.
pitch: This is a dry English sparkling rosé from Hampshire, light and crisp with red cherry fruit and lively bubbles. It's one of our few pink sparklings by the glass, so it's a lovely way to start a meal or toast something without committing to a bottle.
taste: Dry, light and zingy, with red cherry and red berry fruit and fine, lively bubbles.
serve: 6-8°C · flute or tulip-shaped white wine glass

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: Pinot Noir is a classic match for duck, and the fresh bubbles cut through the richness of the terrine.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: The crisp acidity and bubbles clean up the fried batter like a squeeze of lemon.
The zesty freshness lifts the rich, smoky pâté, and the red fruit works well with oily fish.

hook: Pinot Noir from Givry, one of only two red Burgundies we pour by the glass.
pitch: This is a light, fresh red Burgundy with red cherry fruit and an earthy touch, like damp leaves and mushrooms, and very little of that drying grip. It's perfect if you'd like a proper Burgundy by the glass that goes beautifully with duck, mushrooms or chicken.
taste: Light and fresh, with red cherry fruit and a soft earthy note of damp leaves and mushrooms.

dishes.dish: Roast Creedy Carver Duck, Orange Sauce
dishes.why: Duck is a classic match for Pinot Noir, and the wine's freshness lifts the rich meat and the orange sauce.

dishes.dish: Oyster Mushrooms, Scrambled Eggs, Truffle, Toast
dishes.why: The wine's earthy, mushroomy side matches the mushrooms and truffle perfectly.

dishes.dish: Celeriac, Beetroot & Chard Pithivier, Vegetable Gravy
dishes.why: A light, earthy red that sits happily with earthy vegetables and gravy without taking over.

hook: A 2016 Pauillac from Bordeaux's Left Bank, where gravel soils lean the blend towards Cabernet Sauvignon.
pitch: This is a classic, full-bodied Bordeaux with blackcurrant and cedar-wood flavours, a lively freshness and a firm grip, the drying feel you get from strong tea. With a few years in the bottle, it's at its best alongside a fatty cut of beef, which smooths that grip out.
taste: Blackcurrant and cedar wood, with a hint of vanilla and toast, a mouth-watering freshness, and a firm, drying grip on the finish.

dishes.dish: Grilled Wing Rib, Bone Marrow, Parsley Butter
dishes.why: The fat in the beef and bone marrow softens the wine's firm grip, and the grilled flavours suit its cedar and toast.
A rich roast cut of beef is the classic partner for a Cabernet-led Bordeaux, and the meat makes the wine taste smoother.
The fatty beef and melted cheese tame the tannin, so the blackcurrant fruit comes through.

hook: Chardonnay from Sta. Rita Hills, on California's Central Coast, where the vineyards are cooled by the Pacific.
pitch: This is a Californian Chardonnay from Sta. Rita Hills, where cool air off the Pacific keeps it fresh rather than heavy. If you like white Burgundy but fancy trying something from the New World, it's a lovely choice.
taste: Dry and medium-bodied, with fresh citrus fruit and a lively finish.

dishes.why: Chardonnay is a classic match for roast chicken, with enough body for the meat and enough freshness to keep each mouthful lively.
It has the body to match the creamy beans and leeks, but enough freshness for the delicate fish.

dishes.dish: Delica Squash Risotto, Brown Butter, Pumpkin Seed Relish
dishes.why: The wine's medium body sits nicely with a creamy risotto, and its freshness lifts the rich brown butter.

hook: A single-year 2020 pink fizz from Kent, by one of England's classic sparkling houses.
pitch: This is a dry English sparkling rosé from Kent, all from the 2020 harvest, crisp and fresh with red cherry fruit. Gusbourne is one of England's classic sparkling producers, so it's a great bottle for a celebration or to show off what English wine can do.
taste: Dry, light and crisp, with red cherry and red berry fruit and fine, lively bubbles.
serve: 6-8°C · flute or tulip-shaped white wine glass

dishes.dish: Eggs Royale, Hot Smoked Chalk Stream Trout
dishes.why: Pinot Noir loves salmon-like fish such as trout, and the crisp bubbles cut through the creamy hollandaise.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: It's light and zesty enough not to swamp the delicate raw fish, and its acidity matches the lemon.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: Duck and Pinot Noir are a classic pair, and the bubbles refresh the palate after each rich mouthful.

hook: A white Burgundy made from Aligoté, Burgundy's other white grape, rather than Chardonnay.
pitch: This is a crisp, lemony white from Burgundy, made from Aligoté instead of the usual Chardonnay, so it feels bright and mouth-watering rather than rich. If you love fresh, zesty whites with seafood, this is a really interesting Burgundy to try.
taste: Expect a light, crisp white with lemon and green apple and a clean, mouth-watering finish.

dishes.why: Its sharp, lemony freshness works like a squeeze of lemon on salty, delicate oysters.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: A light, crisp white won't swamp the delicate raw fish, and its citrus echoes the preserved lemon.
Its zippy freshness cuts through the rich, smoky pâté and keeps every bite tasting clean.

say: WALL-ter SKOT PEE-noh NWAR, la KOMB VAIRT
hook: Oregon Pinot Noir from the Willamette Valley, said 'wil-AM-it', a cool, wet place with dry summers.
pitch: This is a light, fresh red from Oregon, with red cherry fruit and an earthy, forest-floor edge, and almost no drying grip. It's elegant rather than heavy, so it sits beautifully with duck, mushrooms and richer starters without taking over the plate.
taste: Bright red cherry with an earthy, forest-floor note, light on the palate and refreshingly crisp.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: Pinot Noir is a classic match for duck, and its freshness cuts through the richness of the terrine.

dishes.dish: Oyster Mushrooms, Scrambled Eggs, Truffle, Toast
dishes.why: The wine's earthy, forest-floor side echoes the mushrooms and truffle.
A light, earthy red that won't swamp the creamy gratin but picks up its truffle and root-vegetable flavours.

hook: The oldest red on our list: a 2010 Pessac-Léognan, with years for its tannins to soften.
