pitch: This is a mature Bordeaux, where the blackcurrant fruit has moved towards cedar, tobacco and a pencil-lead note, and the drying grip (tannin) has had time to soften. If you like your red wine savoury and mellow, with real age on it, this is a lovely bottle with roast beef and mushrooms.
taste: Dark fruit turning to cedar, tobacco and a hint of pencil lead, with fresh acidity and a smooth, softened grip.
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant 30 minutes, poured gently in case of sediment (the deposit that settles in older reds)

dishes.dish: Roast Yorkshire Beef Rump, Wild Mushrooms & Gravy
dishes.why: The wine's aged cedar and tobacco notes meet the earthy mushrooms, and the beef keeps it smooth.

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: A rich, slow-cooked beef pie suits a mellow older Bordeaux, and the fat rounds off its tannin.
Roast beef is the classic match for Cabernet-led Bordeaux, letting the savoury aged flavours shine.

hook: Our only Champagne by the glass: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier, rested at least a year on its yeast.
pitch: It's a dry, fresh Champagne with crisp citrus, a hint of red cherry and a creamy feel from time spent resting on its yeast. It's the one Champagne we pour by the glass, so you can have proper Champagne without committing to a whole bottle.
taste: Dry and lively, with crisp citrus and a touch of red cherry, and a soft, creamy texture under the bubbles.
serve: 6-8°C · tulip-shaped Champagne glass or white wine glass

dishes.why: Crisp, citrusy Chardonnay is a classic partner for oysters, and the freshness matches their salty, sea-fresh taste.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: The bubbles and sharp freshness cut straight through the crispy batter, so every mouthful tastes as good as the first.
The fresh acidity lifts the rich, smoky, salty pâté and keeps it from feeling heavy.

say: sha-TOH SMITH oh la-FEET, luh puh-TEE
hook: A Pessac-Léognan red from Bordeaux, where Cabernet Sauvignon usually leads, giving blackcurrant, cedar and a firm grip.
pitch: It's a full, firm red from Pessac-Léognan in Bordeaux, with blackcurrant and cedar and a drying grip, a bit like strong tea, that softens beautifully with red meat. If you're having the beef rump or a steak, it's a classic Bordeaux that makes the meat taste even richer.
taste: Blackcurrant and cedar, with a drying grip like strong tea (that's tannin) and a fresh, mouth-watering edge (that's acidity) that keeps it lively.
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant 30-60 minutes to let it open up

dishes.why: The fat in the roast beef softens the wine's grip, and the blackcurrant fruit flatters the meat.

dishes.dish: Grilled Wing Rib, Bone Marrow, Parsley Butter
dishes.why: Rich grilled beef and bone marrow are exactly what a firm Cabernet-led Bordeaux wants.
A juicy beef burger with melted cheese has the richness to tame the tannin and make the wine feel smoother.

hook: Châteauneuf-du-Pape is one of the Rhône's named crus, special areas that set their own rules.
pitch: This is a full, warming red from the south of France, with ripe red berry fruit and a little white pepper spice. It feels generous and round rather than harsh, so it's lovely with our richest dishes, like the pie for two or the venison.
taste: Ripe red berries and a pinch of white pepper, round and warming, with a gentle grip from the tannin (the drying feel on your gums).
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant 30 to 60 minutes

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: Rhône reds are made for slow-cooked, stew-like dishes, and this one has the weight to match a rich, braised beef pie.
The ripe red berry fruit picks up the blackberries, and the peppery warmth suits the earthy venison.
Roast meats are a classic match for this style, and its soft, round feel works well with roast beef.

hook: From Saint-Julien in Bordeaux's Médoc, where gravel soils usually make Cabernet Sauvignon the lead grape.
pitch: This is a full, firm red from Saint-Julien in Bordeaux, with blackcurrant and cedar and a drying grip, like strong tea, that melts into rich beef. It's a proper classic Bordeaux for anyone sharing the pie or having roast beef.
taste: Blackcurrant and cedar, with a firm, drying grip like strong tea (that's tannin) and a fresh, mouth-watering edge (that's acidity).
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant 30-60 minutes to let it open up

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: Slow-cooked beef and bone marrow are rich enough to soften the wine's grip, and its freshness cuts through the pastry and gravy.

dishes.dish: Roast Yorkshire Beef Rump, Wild Mushrooms & Gravy
dishes.why: Roast beef softens the tannin, and the earthy mushrooms sit nicely with the cedar notes.

dishes.dish: Grilled Wing Rib, Bone Marrow, Parsley Butter
dishes.why: Fatty grilled beef is the classic match for a firm Cabernet-led Bordeaux.

say: SHAN-in PEE-noh NWAR, SAN-tuh REE-tuh HILLS
hook: Californian Pinot Noir from Sta. Rita Hills, on the Central Coast, where the Pacific keeps things cool.
pitch: This is a light, fresh Californian red with red cherry fruit, a hint of earthiness and very little drying grip. It's gentle enough for roast chicken or even fish, so it's a lovely choice when the table wants a red that won't overpower the food.
taste: Juicy red cherry with a light earthy touch, light on the palate with a crisp, refreshing finish.

dishes.why: Roast chicken is a classic Pinot Noir match: a light red that complements the meat rather than drowning it.

dishes.dish: Roast Creedy Carver Duck, Orange Sauce
dishes.why: Pinot Noir is a natural partner for duck, and its freshness balances the rich meat and the orange sauce.
With so little drying grip, it's one of the few reds that can go with fish.

say: LOH-peth deh eh-REH-dee-ah, VEEN-yah ton-DOH-nee-ah, ree-OH-hah
hook: From López de Heredia, a classic Rioja house; Reserva means at least three years' ageing, one in oak.
pitch: It's a mature, savoury Spanish red, where red cherry and plum fruit has softened into leather, tobacco and dried fruit over years of ageing. It comes from one of Rioja's classic houses, so it's a real treat with the Ibérico pork or the charcuterie.
taste: Red cherry and plum with leather, tobacco and dried fruit from age, and a firm, drying grip of tannin on your gums.
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant 30 minutes, pouring gently as an older wine may have sediment (harmless bits at the bottom)

dishes.why: Rioja and Spanish pork are a natural pair, and the savoury, aged flavours suit the rich, slightly sweet meat.
Rioja is a classic match for cured meats like chorizo and jamón, and the tannin handles the salt and fat.
Grilled and roast meats suit Tempranillo, and its firm grip stands up to rich beef.

say: doh-MEN toh-LOH BOHT, shor-AY lay BOHN
hook: Pure Burgundy Pinot Noir, a thin-skinned grape winemakers handle gently, with light oak so the fruit shows.
pitch: This is a light, fresh red Burgundy with red cherry fruit, a gentle earthy note and very little of that drying grip you get from heavier reds. It's lovely with duck or roast chicken and won't weigh you down, so it suits guests who want a red with real finesse rather than power.
taste: Bright red cherry with a soft earthy, damp-woodland note (what wine people call 'forest floor'), light in the mouth and mouth-wateringly fresh.

dishes.dish: Roast Creedy Carver Duck, Orange Sauce
dishes.why: Duck and Pinot Noir are a classic match: the fresh acidity cuts through the rich duck and the cherry fruit sits nicely with the orange sauce.
Roast chicken is one of Pinot Noir's best partners, because a light red like this complements the meat without overpowering it.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: The wine's freshness cleans up the richness of the terrine and its red fruit works with the sweet-spiced chutney.

say: fa-MEE peh-RAN, coat doo ROAN ray-ZAIRV
hook: A Côtes du Rhône, usually led by Grenache: think red berries and a twist of white pepper.
pitch: This is a friendly, medium-weight French red with ripe red berry fruit, a pinch of white pepper and a soft, warming finish. It's easy to enjoy on its own but really comes alive with roast meats and slow-cooked dishes.
taste: Ripe red berries with a pinch of white pepper, soft tannin (the dry, grippy feel red wine leaves in your mouth) and a gentle warmth on the finish.

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: Rhône reds are made for slow-cooked beef, and the ripe fruit and pepper stand up to that rich, braised filling.
The red berry fruit picks up the blackberries and the white pepper flatters the earthy venison.
A classic roast-meat red: soft enough not to fight the beef, with enough fruit to match it.

hook: A Margaux from Bordeaux's Left Bank, where gravel soils favour blends led by Cabernet Sauvignon.
pitch: This is a full, dry Margaux with blackcurrant and cedar, and at 2016 it has had years for its grip to start softening. It's a proper treat with our beef, because the fat in the meat makes the wine feel even smoother.
taste: Dry and full-bodied, meaning it feels weighty in the mouth, with blackcurrant and cedar, a mouth-watering freshness and a firm, drying grip on the gums (that's tannin) that is starting to soften with age.
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant about an hour

dishes.why: The richness of the roasted beef softens the wine's firm tannin, so both taste smoother.

dishes.dish: Grilled Wing Rib, Bone Marrow, Parsley Butter
dishes.why: Grilled steak and bone marrow are exactly the fatty red meat a Cabernet-led Bordeaux is made for.

dishes.dish: Roast Yorkshire Beef Rump, Wild Mushrooms & Gravy
dishes.why: The earthy mushrooms and gravy pick up the cedar and tobacco notes that come with age.

hook: A ten-year-old tawny Port from Portugal's Douro, where tawnies age for many years in wooden cask.
pitch: This is a sweet, mellow Port that tastes of toffee, walnuts and dried fruit, and it is served in a 100ml glass. Time in wooden cask has softened it into something smooth and warming, so it is lovely with pudding, with cheese or on its own to finish the evening.
taste: Sweet and smooth, with caramel, toasted nuts, dried figs and a hint of orange peel.
serve: 12-14°C, lightly chilled · small Port or dessert wine glass

dishes.why: The Port's toffee and walnut flavours echo the honey and walnuts, and it is just as sweet as the pudding.
Its dried-fig and nutty notes sit right alongside the figs and almonds in the tart.

dishes.dish: Neal's Yard Cheese Board, Boozy Fruit Chutney, Oat Cakes & Malt Loaf
dishes.why: Sweet, nutty Port and salty cheese are a classic match, and it loves the fruit chutney and malt loaf too.

say: pee-AIR pie-YAR, lay par-SELL, grahn KROO boo-ZEE
hook: Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from Bouzy, a Grand Cru village, meaning top-rated in Champagne.
pitch: It's a dry, fresh Champagne with real depth: red cherry from Pinot Noir and citrus lift from Chardonnay. The grapes come from Bouzy, one of Champagne's top-rated Grand Cru villages, so it's a serious bottle that can stay at the table through the meal.
taste: Dry and fresh, with red cherry depth and a citrus edge, carried by fine bubbles.
serve: 8-10°C · tulip-shaped Champagne glass or white wine glass

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: Pinot Noir is a classic match for duck, and the bubbles and freshness cut through the rich terrine.

dishes.dish: Oyster Mushrooms, Scrambled Eggs, Truffle, Toast
dishes.why: Pinot Noir loves mushrooms, and the freshness lifts the creamy eggs.
Roast chicken is a natural partner for Pinot Noir, and the Champagne has enough depth to stand up to it.

grapes: Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca, Tinta Roriz
say: KAH-zah feh-ray-REEN-yah, KEEN-tah deh LEH-dah, DOO-roo TEEN-toh
hook: A dry red from the steep Douro terraces that also make Port, usually led by Touriga Nacional.
pitch: It's a dry red from Portugal's Douro, deep and full-bodied, with concentrated dark black fruit and a floral, violet scent. If you want a big red with real grip for the pie, the wing rib or the venison, this is the one, and you can try it by the glass.
taste: Dark black fruit and violets, rich and full, with firm tannin, the drying grip you feel on your gums.
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant 45 minutes for a bottle; not needed for a glass

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: Big Douro reds are made for slow-cooked meat, and the firm grip and dark fruit stand up to the rich beef and marrow.

dishes.dish: Grilled Wing Rib, Bone Marrow, Parsley Butter
dishes.why: The firm tannin cuts through the fat of the beef and bone marrow.
The concentrated black fruit picks up the blackberries and suits the rich, earthy venison.

say: sha-TOH duh mar-sa-NAY, mar-sa-NAY, kloh doo ZHUH
hook: The oldest red Burgundy on our list: a 2016 Pinot Noir with years in bottle.
pitch: This is a light, elegant red Burgundy from 2016, so it has had time in bottle, and good Pinot Noir of this age can move from red cherry towards earthy, mushroomy flavours. It's a great choice for guests who love mature, savoury reds, and it's wonderful with duck or anything with mushrooms or truffle.
taste: Red cherry with earthy notes of damp leaves and mushroom that Pinot Noir can develop with age, light in the mouth and fresh.

dishes.why: The earthy truffle and artichoke pick up the earthy, mushroomy side of an older Pinot Noir, and the wine's freshness cuts the cream.

dishes.dish: Roast Creedy Carver Duck, Orange Sauce
dishes.why: Duck is a classic match for Pinot Noir, and the wine's fresh acidity cuts the richness of the meat.

dishes.dish: Oyster Mushrooms, Scrambled Eggs, Truffle, Toast
dishes.why: Mushrooms and truffle are a natural partner for a Pinot Noir with some age and earthy flavours.

say: sel-va-pee-AH-na, vin SAN-toh del kee-AN-tee ROO-fee-na
hook: A 2015 sweet wine from Chianti Rufina in Tuscany, usually made from Trebbiano and Malvasia grapes.
pitch: This is a sweet Tuscan dessert wine from 2015, and wines in this style usually taste of dried fruit, honey and nuts. It is lovely with our almond and fig puddings or with cheese, and a small glass is a gentle, grown-up way to end the meal.
taste: Sweet and rich, usually with flavours of dried fruit, honey and nuts, kept lively by a little freshness.

dishes.why: The wine's nutty, dried-fruit sweetness picks up the almonds and figs, and the tart's creaminess softens the sweetness.
Honey and walnut are just the flavours this style of wine usually has, so the two taste like they belong together.
A sweet wine against salty, rich cheese is a classic contrast, like cheese with chutney.

hook: Brunello must age at least five years before release, at least two of them in oak.
pitch: This is a savoury Tuscan red with sour cherry, dried herbs and an earthy edge, plus fresh, lively acidity that keeps it bright. It's a 2017, and Brunello ages towards dried cherry, leather and earth, so it's a lovely bottle for rich beef and a proper occasion.
taste: Sour cherry and dried herbs with a savoury, earthy edge, fresh acidity and a firm but not harsh grip, moving with age towards dried cherry, leather and earth.

dishes.dish: Grilled Wing Rib, Bone Marrow, Parsley Butter
dishes.why: Brunello is a classic with grilled steak, and its fresh acidity cuts through the bone marrow and butter.
The savoury, earthy side of the Sangiovese sits beautifully with roasted beef.

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: Its earthy, leathery notes match the slow-braised beef, and the acidity keeps a rich pie from feeling heavy.

hook: Our only fine white Burgundy by the glass, from the village of Saint-Romain.
pitch: This is a Chardonnay from the Burgundy village of Saint-Romain, with fresh citrus and apple and a smooth, rounded feel. It's a lovely way to try a fine white Burgundy without committing to a whole bottle, as we pour it by the 125ml glass or 375ml carafe.
taste: Expect a medium-bodied, fresh white with lemon, apple and a smooth, rounded finish.

dishes.why: Roast chicken is a classic match for Chardonnay, and this one has enough body for the savoury meat while staying fresh.
Its citrus freshness suits the delicate white fish, and its smooth feel matches the creamy beans and leeks.

dishes.dish: Delica Squash Risotto, Brown Butter, Pumpkin Seed Relish
dishes.why: Its rounded texture sits nicely with the creamy risotto, and its freshness stops the brown butter feeling heavy.

say: doh-MEN kwah-YOH, zhev-RAY sham-ber-TAN vee-AY VEEN-yuh
hook: Vieilles Vignes means old vines, and Gevrey-Chambertin is village-level Burgundy, one step below Premier Cru.
pitch: This is a red Burgundy made from Pinot Noir: light and fresh, with red cherry and an earthy note like damp leaves on a forest floor. It has real flavour without being heavy, so it sits beautifully alongside duck, chicken or anything with mushrooms or truffle.
taste: Light and fresh, with red cherry, an earthy smell like damp leaves, and very little of that drying grip on your gums.

dishes.why: A light, fresh red like this lifts roast chicken without drowning it.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: Pinot Noir and duck are a classic pair, and the wine's freshness cuts through the richness of the terrine.
The earthy, forest-floor side of the wine picks up the truffle and root vegetables.

say: san soh-VUR, blonk duh BLONK, prem-YAY KROO
hook: Champagne made only from Chardonnay, a white grape. That's what Blanc de Blancs means.
pitch: This is a crisp, lean Champagne made only from Chardonnay, with fresh citrus and a creamy feel from time spent resting on its yeast. It's lovely with oysters or anything from the sea, and Premier Cru on the label means the grapes come from villages rated in Champagne's second-highest tier.
taste: Fresh lemony citrus and sharp, mouth-watering freshness, with a soft, creamy texture under the bubbles.

dishes.why: Lean, citrusy Chardonnay is a classic with oysters, and the fresh bubbles match their salty, sea-fresh taste.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: Its crisp citrus freshness echoes the preserved lemon and doesn't swamp the delicate raw fish.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: The bubbles and sharp freshness cut through the batter and make every bite feel lighter.

say: doh-MEN dew sha-TOH fee-LEEP luh ar-DEE, san-toh-BAN, on ves-VOH
hook: A 2022 Burgundy Chardonnay from the village of Saint-Aubin, with the site name En Vesveau on the label.
pitch: This is a dry white Burgundy made from Chardonnay, fresh and mouth-watering, with citrus and orchard fruit and a smooth, medium weight. It's a proper step up from the house Mâcon, elegant enough for a special meal without being heavy.
taste: Dry and fresh, with lemon and apple-like fruit, a mouth-watering finish and a smooth, medium-weight feel in the mouth.

dishes.why: White Burgundy suits white fish, and its freshness keeps the creamy beans and leeks tasting light.
Roast chicken is a classic match for Chardonnay, and this has enough body to stand up to it without overpowering it.

dishes.dish: Delica Squash Risotto, Brown Butter, Pumpkin Seed Relish
dishes.why: The wine's smooth texture sits nicely with the creamy risotto, and its freshness cuts through the brown butter.

say: sha-TOH lay-oh-VEEL pwah-feh-RAY, pa-vee-YON duh lay-oh-VEEL pwah-feh-RAY
hook: A Saint-Julien from the Médoc's gravel, where blends usually lean on Cabernet Sauvignon's blackcurrant and cedar.
pitch: This is a full, dry Saint-Julien from 2019, with blackcurrant, cedar and a firm, youthful grip. With our richest beef dishes that grip melts into the meat and the whole thing tastes generous.
taste: Dry and full-bodied, meaning it feels weighty in the mouth, with blackcurrant, cedar and a touch of vanilla and toast, a mouth-watering freshness and a firm, drying grip on the gums (that's tannin).
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant about an hour, to soften the young tannin

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: All that braised beef and marrow fat softens the wine's young tannin, and its freshness cuts through the richness.

dishes.dish: Grilled Wing Rib, Bone Marrow, Parsley Butter
dishes.why: Grilled steak is the classic partner for a Cabernet-led Bordeaux, and the fat smooths out the grip.
The rich roasted beef stands up to a full red and makes the tannin feel softer.

hook: From Central Otago, the world's most southerly wine region, made by one of its classic producers.
pitch: This is a Pinot Noir from New Zealand: light and fresh, with red cherry and an earthy note like damp leaves on a forest floor. It's lively enough to cut through rich dishes like duck or venison but gentle enough not to drown them.
taste: Light and lively, with red cherry, an earthy forest-floor note and only a soft, gentle grip.

dishes.dish: Roast Creedy Carver Duck, Orange Sauce
dishes.why: Pinot Noir is a classic with duck, and its freshness cuts through the rich meat and sweet sauce.
The red cherry fruit and earthy notes sit nicely with the venison, celeriac and blackberries.

dishes.dish: Celeriac, Beetroot & Chard Pithivier, Vegetable Gravy
dishes.why: An earthy dish meets the earthy, forest-floor side of the wine, and it's light enough not to swamp the vegetables.

hook: A 2016 Napa red, grown with warm days and fog-cooled nights off San Pablo Bay.
pitch: This is a big, rich Napa red, usually led by Cabernet Sauvignon, with blackcurrant, cedar and a toasty, vanilla edge, and as a 2016 it has had time to start mellowing. If you're having the steak or the beef, it's a proper celebration bottle that stands up to every mouthful.
taste: Ripe blackcurrant and dark fruit with cedar, vanilla and toast, and a firm, drying grip that age is starting to soften towards cedar and tobacco.
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant 30 minutes (pour it into a decanter, a glass jug, so it can breathe)

dishes.dish: Grilled Wing Rib, Bone Marrow, Parsley Butter
dishes.why: The fat in the beef and bone marrow softens the wine's grip, and the char loves its cedar and toast.
Rich roast beef is exactly what a big Cabernet-style red wants, and the wine's freshness keeps each bite lively.

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: This rich, slow-cooked beef pie has the weight to match a full-bodied red like this one.

hook: A pink Champagne blending Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Pinot Meunier, grown in Champagne's barely-ripening cool climate.
pitch: This is a dry pink Champagne with red cherry fruit from Pinot Noir and a crisp, fresh finish. It's lively enough to start the meal but has the fruit to stand up to duck, roast chicken or trout.
taste: Red cherry and berry fruit with crisp, mouth-watering freshness and a dry, clean finish.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: Pinot Noir is a natural with duck, and the bubbles and freshness cut through the rich terrine.
The red cherry fruit suits roast chicken, the same way a light Pinot Noir does.

dishes.dish: Eggs Royale, Hot Smoked Chalk Stream Trout
dishes.why: Pinot Noir goes well with salmon-like fish, and the crisp bubbles lift the rich, creamy eggs.

hook: Northern Rhône Syrah, black pepper and blackberry, grown in the valley's cooler, continental north.
pitch: This is a deep, dark Syrah from the north of France's Rhône Valley, full of blackberry and black pepper with a smoky edge. It has a good firm grip, so it's made for grilled meat and game like our venison.
taste: Blackberry and black pepper with a smoky edge, deep colour and a firm, drying grip.

dishes.why: Syrah loves game, and its blackberry fruit echoes the blackberries on the plate.
The firm grip and peppery flavour stand up well to rich roasted beef.

dishes.dish: Grilled Wing Rib, Bone Marrow, Parsley Butter
dishes.why: Syrah is a natural with grilled meat, and the smoky notes suit the char on the beef.

say: doh-MEN duh mon-TEE, BOHN pruh-MYAIR KROO, lay see-ZEE
hook: A Beaune Premier Cru: Burgundy's second-highest tier, just below Grand Cru, from the Les Sizies vineyard.
pitch: It's a light, fresh red Burgundy with red cherry fruit and a gentle earthy, woodland edge, so it never feels heavy. As a Premier Cru, one level below Burgundy's very top, it's a proper treat that still sits happily alongside roast chicken or duck.
taste: Bright red cherry with a hint of forest floor (an earthy, damp-leaves smell), light on the tongue with a fresh, mouth-watering finish.

dishes.why: Roast chicken is a classic match for Pinot Noir: the wine's freshness lifts the meat without swamping it.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: Duck and Pinot Noir are old friends, and the wine's red cherry fruit sits nicely with the pear chutney.
The wine's earthy, mushroomy side matches the truffle, and its freshness cuts through the creamy gratin.

say: fa-MEE peh-RAN, mor-GON, coat doo PEE
hook: A Morgon from Beaujolais: Gamay grape, bright strawberry and cherry, lovely served lightly chilled.
pitch: This is a lighter red bursting with bright strawberry and cherry fruit, with soft tannin and a fresh, juicy feel. We serve it lightly chilled, so it's brilliant with charcuterie, roast chicken or anyone who finds most reds too heavy.
taste: Bright, juicy strawberry and cherry with soft tannin (very little of that dry, grippy feel) and a fresh finish.

dishes.why: Gamay is a classic with cured meats: the juicy red fruit and soft tannin refresh you between salty, rich slices.
Light reds like this are made for roast chicken, with enough fruit to flatter it without overpowering it.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: The bright cherry fruit lifts the rich terrine and sits nicely with the sweet chutney.

say: jee-DEE VY-rah, ba-ROH-loh, KOSS-teh dee ROH-zeh
hook: By law, Barolo ages at least 38 months before release, with 18 of those in wood.
pitch: This is Barolo, made from Nebbiolo: it looks quite pale, but it's powerful, with aromas of tar and rose petals, a firm drying grip and fresh, mouthwatering acidity. It's a proper occasion bottle for braised beef or venison, and we'll decant it so it opens up in the glass.
taste: Tar and rose petals with a firm, drying grip on the gums and mouthwatering freshness, far more powerful than its pale colour suggests.

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: Braised beef is a classic match for Barolo, and the wine's grip and freshness cut through the rich bone marrow.
Nebbiolo loves game, and its tar and rose notes sit beautifully with the earthy venison.
Truffle is one of Barolo's favourite partners, and the wine's acidity freshens up the creamy gratin.

hook: Made by Domaine Laroche, the same house behind our Chablis Grand Cru Les Blanchots: Burgundy Chardonnay.
pitch: This is Chablis, Chardonnay from Burgundy, in a lean, fresh, citrusy style rather than a rich, buttery one. If you like a crisp, clean white, you'll love it with oysters and white fish.
taste: Lean, fresh and citrusy, with lively, mouth-watering acidity.

dishes.why: A lean, fresh Chardonnay is a classic with salty, delicate raw oysters.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: The wine's citrus freshness matches the preserved lemon and lets the delicate fish shine.
White fish and shellfish love a crisp Chardonnay, and its acidity keeps the creamy sauce feeling light.

say: zhon no-EL gan-YAR, sha-SAN-yuh mon-ra-SHAY, lay ma-ZOOR
hook: Chardonnay from Chassagne-Montrachet in Burgundy, with the site name Les Masures on the label, 2023 vintage.
pitch: This is a dry white Burgundy from Chassagne-Montrachet, one of the most famous names for Chardonnay, with a fuller, rounder feel and a fresh, mouth-watering finish. It's a real treat with roast chicken or anything creamy, and it's still young, with years of life ahead of it.
taste: Dry, with ripe citrus and orchard fruit, a rich, rounded feel in the mouth and a fresh finish that keeps it from feeling heavy.

dishes.why: Roast chicken and fuller white Burgundy are a classic pairing, and the wine's weight matches the bird.
The wine's rounded texture goes with the creamy gratin, and its freshness lifts the rich, earthy flavours.
Chardonnay suits white fish in a creamy sauce, and there's enough freshness to keep the dish tasting light.

say: fee-lee-po-NAH, blonk duh NWAR, EX-truh BROOT
hook: A white Champagne made only from black Pinot Noir grapes, all from the single 2018 harvest.
pitch: This is a very dry Champagne made entirely from Pinot Noir, so it's crisp and refreshing with a little red-cherry depth behind the bubbles. It comes from one year, 2018, and it's brilliant with oysters or anything salty and fresh.
taste: Very dry and crisp, with a hint of red cherry from the Pinot Noir and a clean, refreshing finish.

dishes.why: It's very dry and fresh, so it matches the salty oysters and the sharp shallot vinegar without tasting thin.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: The crisp acidity (the mouth-watering freshness) sits nicely alongside the lemon and keeps the delicate raw fish tasting clean.

dishes.dish: Oyster Mushrooms, Scrambled Eggs, Truffle, Toast
dishes.why: Pinot Noir loves mushrooms, and the bubbles freshen up the creamy eggs between bites.

hook: Bollinger is one of Champagne's classic houses, named alongside Krug and Veuve Clicquot.
pitch: This is Bollinger's house Champagne, a dry blend led by Pinot Noir with Chardonnay and Pinot Meunier, so it's fresh and lively with a little red-fruit depth. It's a famous name that tastes as good as it sounds, and it's lovely with fish and chips.
taste: Dry and crisp, with a hint of red cherry from the Pinot Noir and a fresh, lively sparkle.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: The bubbles and crisp acidity (the mouth-watering freshness) cut through the fried batter and keep every bite tasting fresh.

dishes.dish: Eggs Royale, Hot Smoked Chalk Stream Trout
dishes.why: Pinot Noir loves smoked fish, and the fresh sparkle lifts the rich, creamy hollandaise.
Its freshness cleans up the rich, smoky, salty pâté so you want another bite.

hook: Pink Champagne made from all three Champagne grapes: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Pinot Meunier.
pitch: This is a pink Champagne that's dry and crisp, with red cherry fruit from the Pinot Noir in the blend. It's fresh enough to start the evening with, and has enough fruit to keep going with the duck terrine or the charcuterie.
taste: Dry and refreshing, with a gentle red cherry fruitiness and a clean, lively finish.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: Pinot Noir loves duck, and the bubbles and freshness cut through the richness of the terrine.
The crisp, fresh taste cleans up the salt and fat of the cured meats, and the red fruit goes well with them.

dishes.dish: Eggs Royale, Hot Smoked Chalk Stream Trout
dishes.why: Pinot Noir is a classic match for salmon-style fish, so a pink Champagne with smoked trout makes a lovely brunch treat.

say: roh-BAIR shuh-vee-YON, NWEE san ZHORZH, vyay VEEN-yuh
hook: A Nuits-Saint-Georges from old vines, which is what 'Vieilles Vignes' on the label means.
pitch: It's a red Burgundy made from Pinot Noir: red cherry fruit with an earthy, woodland side, fresh and light rather than heavy. It's a lovely choice with duck, venison or mushrooms, as it brings out the flavour of the food instead of drowning it.
taste: Red cherry with forest-floor notes (an earthy, damp-leaves smell), light in weight with a fresh, lively finish.

dishes.dish: Roast Creedy Carver Duck, Orange Sauce
dishes.why: Duck is one of Pinot Noir's best partners, and the wine's freshness cuts through the rich meat and sweet orange sauce.
The wine's earthy notes suit the venison and celeriac, and its red cherry fruit sits nicely with the blackberries.

dishes.dish: Roast Yorkshire Beef Rump, Wild Mushrooms & Gravy
dishes.why: Mushrooms are a classic match for Pinot Noir's earthy, woodland side.

hook: From the Haut-Médoc, on Bordeaux's gravelly Left Bank, where blends usually lean on Cabernet Sauvignon.
pitch: This is a young, proper Bordeaux red, full of blackcurrant and cedar with a firm, drying grip. With a rich cut of beef that grip softens and the fruit opens up, so every mouthful of meat makes the wine taste better.
taste: Blackcurrant and cedar wood, full in the mouth, with fresh acidity (a mouth-watering zing) and firm tannin, the drying grip you feel on your gums.
serve: 16-18°C · large red glass · decant about 1 hour, as it is young and firm

dishes.dish: Grilled Wing Rib, Bone Marrow, Parsley Butter
dishes.why: The fat in the beef and bone marrow softens the wine's firm grip, so both taste richer and smoother.
Roast red meat is the classic partner for a Cabernet-led Bordeaux, and the meat's richness tames the tannin.

dishes.dish: Hereford Short Rib, Brisket & Bone Marrow Pie
dishes.why: A rich, slow-cooked beef pie needs a red with this much structure to stand up to it.

say: zhuh-NOH boo-lahn-ZHAY, poo-lee-NYEE mon-rah-SHAY, lay noh-RWAH
hook: Chardonnay from Puligny-Montrachet in Burgundy, named after one vineyard plot: Les Nosroyes.
pitch: This is a dry Chardonnay from Puligny-Montrachet, one of Burgundy's best-known white wine villages, with fresh, lively acidity and a rounder, fuller feel than a crisp everyday white. It's a proper treat with roast chicken or anything in a creamy, buttery sauce, and it's a 2023, so it's bright and youthful now.
taste: A dry white with fresh, mouth-watering acidity (the crisp, zingy part of a wine) and a smooth, rounded texture; any creamy or buttery hint comes from how the winemaker made it.

dishes.why: Burgundy Chardonnay and roast chicken are a classic pairing, and the wine's freshness cuts through the rich, savoury meat.
The wine's smooth texture matches the creamy sauce, while its acidity keeps the delicate fish tasting fresh.

dishes.dish: Delica Squash Risotto, Brown Butter, Pumpkin Seed Relish
dishes.why: A rounder white Burgundy sits happily with the creamy, nutty risotto and brown butter without being drowned out.

say: doh-MEN la-ROSH, sha-BLEE gron KROO, lay blon-SHOH
hook: Our only Grand Cru white: Burgundy's top vineyard tier, from the Les Blanchots vineyard in Chablis.
pitch: This is Chablis from a Grand Cru vineyard, which means the very top of Burgundy's four-step quality ranking, so it's the most serious still white Chablis we pour. It's a dry Chardonnay with crisp, fresh acidity, lovely with oysters or delicate fish, and a real special-occasion bottle.
taste: A dry, crisp white with high, fresh acidity (the zingy, mouth-watering part of a wine) and a long finish.

dishes.why: The wine's crisp acidity matches the salty, sharp oysters and keeps every mouthful fresh.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: A fresh, crisp white lets the delicate raw fish shine and echoes the lemon.
Its acidity lifts the creamy sauce and suits the white fish and mussels.

say: da-VEED mo-RAY, mer-SOH, soo la VELL
hook: Pure Chardonnay from Meursault in Burgundy, by David Moret, who also makes our Saint-Romain and Aligoté.
pitch: This is a rich, rounded white Burgundy from Meursault, made from Chardonnay, with a smooth, creamy feel and a fresh finish. It's a real treat with roast chicken or anything in a creamy sauce, and it's the white to choose for a celebration.
taste: Full and rounded, with ripe citrus and orchard fruit, a smooth, creamy feel and a clean, fresh finish.

dishes.why: Rich white Burgundy and roast chicken are a classic pairing, as the wine's fullness matches the savoury, roasted meat.
The wine's creamy feel suits the creamy beans and leeks, and its freshness keeps the delicate fish lively.

dishes.dish: Delica Squash Risotto, Brown Butter, Pumpkin Seed Relish
dishes.why: A full, smooth Chardonnay sits nicely with a creamy risotto and the nutty brown butter.

say: doh-MEN zhahn-mark bwah-YOH, vol-NAY prem-YAIR KROO, ka-REL soo la sha-PEL
hook: A Volnay Premier Cru: the second of Burgundy's four quality tiers, which are ranked by vineyard site.
pitch: This is a light, fresh Pinot Noir from Burgundy, with red cherry fruit, gentle tannin (the drying grip you feel on your gums) and a hint of forest floor. It's our most special red Burgundy, elegant rather than heavy, so it flatters duck and chicken instead of swamping them.
taste: Light and fresh, with red cherry, a soft, gentle grip and an earthy, forest-floor edge.

dishes.dish: Roast Creedy Carver Duck, Orange Sauce
dishes.why: Duck is a classic match for Pinot Noir, and the wine's fresh acidity (the mouth-watering zing) cuts the richness without fighting the orange.

dishes.dish: Duck & Pancetta Terrine, Spiced Pear Chutney, Toast
dishes.why: The wine's red cherry fruit sits nicely with the chutney, and its lightness keeps a rich terrine feeling fresh.
Roast chicken and Pinot Noir are a natural pair; the wine is light enough not to overpower the meat.

hook: Every grape comes from the 2013 harvest, and vintage Champagne must age at least three years.
pitch: This is a vintage Champagne, meaning all the grapes come from one year, 2013, and it's made from Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. It's dry and crisp, with the extra depth that comes from longer ageing, so it's a real celebration bottle that's brilliant with oysters or crab.
taste: Dry and crisp, with fresh fruit and a deeper, more layered taste than a younger Champagne.

dishes.why: The crisp, fresh taste matches the salty oysters and stands up to the sharp shallot vinegar.

dishes.dish: Curried Crab on Malt Rye & Beer Bread
dishes.why: The bubbles and freshness lift the rich crab and calm the gentle spice.

dishes.dish: Fish & Chips, Crushed Peas, Tartare Sauce
dishes.why: Champagne with fish and chips is a classic: the bubbles and freshness cut right through the batter.

hook: A 2007 vintage Champagne made only from Chardonnay, and the oldest Champagne on our list.
pitch: This is pure Chardonnay Champagne from a single year, 2007, so it has had many years to gain nutty, toasty depth while staying fresh and lemony. If you're marking something special, this is the most remarkable bottle of bubbles we pour.
taste: Expect lemony freshness wrapped in nutty, toasty notes from age and a creamy texture from long resting on the yeast.
serve: 8-10°C · white wine glass or tulip-shaped flute

dishes.why: Chardonnay without oak is a classic match for oysters, and the wine's freshness lifts their salty, delicate taste.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: Its lemony acidity mirrors the preserved lemon, while the toasty depth gives the raw fish a richer frame.
White fish suits Chardonnay, and the wine's creamy texture sits nicely with the creamy beans and leeks.
